If it codes PR1=1 the sequence collapses and pricing is orthogonal to mechanism rather than a stage of it. CORRECTED from 1 to P on Coudy 1957, now a pinned source. THE GRADING IS REAL: the 1689 edict fixes fourteen classes in five-year bands (first to age 5 accomplished, last from 65) and declares interest progressive - du denier 20 au denier 8 dans les treizieme et quatorzieme classes, i.e. 5 per cent rising to 12.5 per cent for the oldest. 1696 adds a fifteenth class from 70; 1709 has twenty. BUT THE GRADING IS NOT ACTUARIAL: Coudy gives the purpose as 'dans un but d'equite' and states flatly that 'l'on ne disposait d'aucune table de mortalite. L'on ne s'en souciait guere non plus' - no mortality table existed and nobody much minded. He doubts the Crown grasped the real cost. So the peril is priced ex ante by age band and NOT from any distribution, which is P and not 1 - the same reading as sea_loan PR1=P, where Harris finds crude pricing sufficient. DECISIVE FOR DIRECTION: Deparcieux (1746) DERIVED survival probabilities by observing the 1689 and 1696 tontines, so the actuarial knowledge came out of these instruments rather than into them.

一、初会 満会迄…都合拾三ヶ年半ニ満会相成候事 — forty-one rounds over thirteen and a half years to 満会.
Same two-tier gap as ko_usui_bango_1822. The 仕法帳 cover names the drafters 世話方, and 米谷 notes 銀預り were sometimes so called — the steward role is emic and has no cell.
大満院 is a 子院 within 誉田八幡宮. 初会 inferred as 文政11 (1828) from the per-round 掛銀 schedule; the tenth round fell in 天保4 (1833).3.

As ko_usui_bango_1822: 米谷 finds rules one to five substantially identical to that association's, and the 掛銀 and 当選銀 schedules nearly the same, because 岡田伊左衛門 and 塩野久右衛門 served as 銀預り and drafted the 仕法 for both. Alternating allocation therefore inherited, and equally inexpressible.

Contributions mutualised among members with no outsider taking the risk, so Harris's category holds on structure. But see PY3 and the CN1 note: this form retains almost nothing of the mutual-aid rationale, and 並松 places it with 富籤 as 無尽本来の特徴である救済的あるいは相互扶助的な金融組織から著しく逸脱したもの.

THE CELL THAT SEPARATES IT FROM THE VILLAGE FORMS. 並松: the 講元(世話人) recruits 血縁・地縁にまったく関係なく、広く講員を募って — with no kin or locality tie whatever. Membership is constituted purely by subscription. Contrast the village kō, where 松永 finds kō built on 親戚・知人・取引相手・信仰.
辻六郎左衛門's 無尽仕法帳 of 文政7年8月 is a 十年・六〇人の取退無尽 — sixty members over ten years, with 備後町三丁目銭屋源兵衛 named as 世話方. One documented instance; the general case is not enumerated.
Open subscription, canvassed widely.

CHARACTERISTIC INADEQUATE — the timing is right and the duration is unexpressible. Contributions fall due periodically, so ex-ante-periodic is correct as far as it goes. But the defining feature of this form is that a member who wins is 次回以降の掛戻義務から免れ — released from all further contribution — while the kō continues on the 未当籤講員. In every other coded association (池田's 持寄融通社, 米谷's 伴吾講 and 四拾人講) the winner keeps paying 空掛 to 満会. CN1 asks when contributions fall due and is silent on how long a member owes them. See logbook 6.
Equal periodic 掛金 per share, as in the other forms. Not separately attested for this variant.
A draw irrespective of loss, as with the other rotating forms.
Entitlement is positional: one draw per member, then exit from the obligation.

抽籤 — lot, not bid. NOTE THE CONSEQUENCE: because allocation is by lot, the liquidity-transfer mechanism that operates in bidding kō is absent here. This form is regressive for a different reason, namely that an early draw yields far more relative to contributions than a late one — 当籤が早ければ掛金額に比して給付額が多くなり、遅ければその逆 — which 並松 calls 射倖性が非常に強い. Lot removes the sorting by urgency and replaces it with sorting by chance.

CAPPED, and the cap is what keeps the form alive. 当籤者に対する給付額が講金のすべてというわけではなく、講金の一部を給付することによって、組織としての持続性が保たれる — the winner receives only part of the pot, and the retained remainder is what allows the association to continue once winners stop contributing.
十年 in 辻六郎左衛門's 仕法帳. A closed run, though shorter than the village cycles.

No peril is priced; nothing resembling one is pooled. 中川 records that one ground for prosecution was the 講元 taking 幕府規定の利子制限をはるかに超える高利潤 — returns far above the shogunate's interest ceilings — so credit was priced, and priced abusively. Peril was not, and there is none here.
Same convenor-plus-steward gap as the other Japanese associations. 中川 names 銭屋源兵衛 as 世話方 for 辻's kō; 並松 uses 講元(世話人) interchangeably. No value expresses an insider-organiser distinct from a steward.
No peril pooled, so no correlation to report. As the other Japanese forms.

HELD OPEN DELIBERATELY. The flood-spreading reading is the received view in the Japanese literature (Furushima 1939; Aono 1982), built on individual village studies. Brown 2006 tests it regionally with GIS and concludes that flood and landslide frequency 'must be seen as insufficient causes by themselves, even if scholars ultimately see them as necessary conditions'. Coding pooling here would enter a contested orthodoxy as data; coding 0 or allocation would enter Brown's negative as a positive. See logbook 6 and vault [[Brown tests equality where a risk reading predicts dispersion]].
Participation follows village membership and shareholding within the village, not kinship, occupation or contract. Iwade's shares were fixed at sixteen by the end of the seventeenth century.

Sixteen shares, fixed by the late seventeenth century and constant thereafter; each wari was generally divided into sixteen sections for which lots were drawn. NOTE: the share count did not track the number of families, so 'membership' is a share, not a household.

A shareholder could not opt out of a redistribution once the village conducted one — but see the hikikuji note at PY2. Coded medium because the source of the obligation varied: some domains (Kaga) regulated joint control by law, elsewhere the practice was village initiative, and Brown 2006 argues for 'local, village-level human agency'.

INAPPLICABLE, AND STRUCTURALLY IMPORTANT. Warichi has no contribution stream and accumulates no fund. It reallocates an existing asset rather than assembling one. Every other form in this census — averia_pool, general_average, the tanomoshi associations, the tontines — collects something. This is the cell on which warichi is unlike all of them, and it is why the pooling category sits awkwardly.
Inapplicable: no contribution to measure. Propagates from CN1.
Inapplicable: no contribution to enforce. Propagates from CN1.

NOT RECORDED BECAUSE THE TEST WAS INCONCLUSIVE. Brown mapped 113 villages (110 geolocated) against elevation and drainage and found anomalies: the Shindōri, Kamegai and Sekiya intervals near the Shinano mouth 'cannot be explained by readily apparent natural conditions', Iwade practises warichi while 'removed from a large hydrological system and floodplain', and most of the sample lies above 67.5 metres. Coding a correlation value here would assert what he could not establish.
Not addressed. Flood and landslide are indifferent to the defence mounted, which would suggest 0, but Brown does not treat responsiveness and the hazard's role is itself unsettled (HZ1).

CHARACTERISTIC FITS AWKWARDLY. Each shareholder receives an allocation by lot irrespective of any loss suffered, which is individual-draw. But unlike every rotating form in this census, ALL members draw simultaneously at each redistribution rather than one member per round — there is no queue and no 'turn'. The value is right about the trigger and wrong about the structure.
Entitlement follows the redistribution cycle rather than a realised loss or a life event. Same caveat as PY0: the cycle allocates to everyone at once.

THE BEST-ATTESTED CELL. Allocation by drawn lot: the village kept 'Lot Exchange Notebooks' (kujikae chō), and in 1756-1757 the sixteen shares were organised into nine lot-drawing groups (kujigumi). CAVEAT WITH NO CELL OF ITS OWN: hikikuji, the right to withhold land from redistribution, ran from under 2 per cent of village land in 1756-57 to 14 per cent in 1818, exceeded the 5 per cent Kaga permitted, and 'the rights to withhold were concentrated in a few hands, not universally shared'. An opt-out from the allocation mechanism has no representation in this vocabulary.
Inapplicable: there is no fund and therefore no surplus on which a residual claim could be held. Propagates from CN1.

Brown describes redistribution outcomes as 'a product of discussion and consensus building during each redistribution', and 2006 concludes for 'an important role for local, village-level human agency'. Contrast the Japanese rotating associations, where a 講元 convenes and a 銀預り administers.

Periodic redistribution at village-specific intervals — five years in the four Nadachi coastal villages, ten in the nine upstream, with a full interval series compiled for 113 villages. The interval is the parameter Brown devotes a chapter to measuring, and on a resetting reading it is the only free parameter the institution has.
Terminal distribution not addressed; the cycle repeats rather than terminating. Warichi ended with the Meiji land tax reform rather than by internal completion.
Inapplicable: no advance is made, so nothing secures one.

OBSERVED ABSENCE. Nothing is priced anywhere in the institution — no premium, no bid, no interest, no ex-ante valuation of the peril. Land was assessed for quality when wari sections were laid out, but that is a measurement of the asset, not a price on a peril. Consistent with every pooling form in the census except the age-classed tontine.

NO FITTING VALUE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Harris's three mechanisms — allocation, spreading, pooling — are all ways of moving a loss. Particular average moves it nowhere: the damage 'falls to the owner of the damaged goods on account of the maxim casum sentit dominum'. It is the null against which the other three are defined, not a fourth alternative. Not coded 'allocation': that value means risk assigned to a named party BY CONTRACT, whereas this is a default rule operating in the absence of any arrangement.

THE DISCRIMINATING CELL AGAINST general_average. Peril loss stays with the owner of the damaged goods. Contrast general_average RB1=all-stakeholders. Same voyage, same hull, same peril — and the incidence turns entirely on whether the damage was 'consciously sought out with the intention of avoiding a more serious one' (general) or came 'from an irresistible or unforeseeable external cause' (particular).
Market risk likewise remains with the goods' owner; nothing in the doctrine transfers it. Coded medium: the sources address peril, not price.

No advance is made, so nothing secures one. NOTE the contractual override: Zanini shows that under a bottomry contract, particular-average damage reduced the borrower's repayment obligation proportionally, 'since the relative risk had been transferred to the lender'. The default rule is displaceable by contract, and the sea loan is one instrument that displaces it.
Inapplicable: no obligation is advanced, so none is discharged. See the bottomry note at RB3 for the contractual case, which belongs to sea_loan rather than here.
Inapplicable: there is no fund and no output. Nothing is collected and nothing is distributed.
Inapplicable: propagates from PY0.
Inapplicable: propagates from PY0.
Inapplicable: no contribution is levied at any time, before or after the event. This is the cell on which particular average differs from general_average (ex-post-assessment) most starkly.
Inapplicable: propagates from CN1.
Inapplicable: propagates from CN1.
Inapplicable: there is no membership to join, voluntarily or otherwise. Whoever owns damaged goods bears the damage; no one participates.
Inapplicable: no pool exists whose exhaustion could raise the question.
Inapplicable: there is no contribution beyond which liability could extend. The owner's exposure is his goods, entire.

UNSETTLED, AND THE INTERESTING CELL. A particular-average loss requires no verification within the sharing institution, since nothing is shared. But the CLASSIFICATION does — Dreijer notes the distinction was drawn 'particularly for insurers as they had to distinguish between the two to determine their contribution to damages'. So verification attaches to the boundary rather than to the loss, and VF1 has no way to say so. Addobbati holds the boundary itself unverifiable: deliberateness is 'an internal act' attested only by 'the master who makes the damage declaration'.

No peril is priced, because no peril is transferred. Consistent with general_average PR1=0 and averia_pool PR1=0 — the whole family prices nothing ex ante — but here for the opposite reason: not because calculation is deferred to an ex-post assessment, but because there is no assessment at all.
Inapplicable: a default rule of loss incidence has no duration. Contrast general_average DR1=single-event, which is struck for one voyage and one sacrifice.

Not recorded. The doctrine is indifferent to whether the peril is idiosyncratic or covariate; it turns on human causality against external randomness, which is a different axis from correlation across members.

NO FITTING VALUE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Allocation, spreading and pooling all presuppose that a loss is being moved among parties with a stake. Here nothing is mitigated: 小林 finds the association was 強制的に組織して返済を期待せず直接藩財政に入れてしまった — compulsorily organised, no repayment expected, receipts going straight into domain finances — and calls it 献金講 とも呼ぶべきもの, a donation kō, 御未進取立講に近い仕法. A kō in form and a levy in function. Third form in this census whose MC1 cannot be set (with warichi_iwade and particular_average).

Membership follows residence on the Iino domain's portion of 長興寺村 rather than kinship, occupation or subscription. Both 高持 and 無高 households were enrolled — some 100 persons for a village assessment of roughly 166 koku.

強制的に集めた. 小林 reads the domain's ability to compel a hundred-odd members as evidence that 藩権力の余力がまだ多少残っていた. COMPULSION WAS RESISTIBLE, THOUGH: neighbouring 岡部藩 ordered compulsory enrolment in a クジ頼母子 across four districts in 寛政3 (1791) and the villages refused, pleading 凶作による困窮, and likewise refused a 用金 levy of 2両 per 100石.

Twice yearly in the fourth and ninth months for this association; the preceding 御殿様頼母子講 met always in the eleventh. 小林 reads the 大黒屋 timing as accommodating the agricultural calendar somewhat more than its predecessor.

NO FITTING VALUE — THE ASSESSMENT IS A TWO-PART TARIFF AND CN2 ADMITS ONE BASIS. Contributions divide into 高割 (proportional to assessed landholding, 2匁5分 down to 8分 per koku by year) PLUS 家割 (a flat per-household charge of 3匁, 2匁2分2厘, 1匁9分, 1匁5分). Neither 'equal' nor 'proportional-to-stake' describes the sum, and the interaction between the two parts is precisely where the regressivity lives — see the note at LM-TTTT-06. A composite assessment has no representation in this vocabulary.

THE SUBSTANTIVE FINDING, RECORDED HERE FOR WANT OF A CELL FOR IT. The landless paid no 高掛り but were charged 家割 — and 無高上層 were charged 1分 to 2分2厘 MORE flat charge than 高持百姓, with a further 無高下 stratum below them paying 8分 to 1匁 less than 無高上層. 小林's own verdict: 石高が多いほど実質的な負担は少なくなり、無高ほど実質的な負担が多くなる。すなわち累進ではなくて逆進となってまことに不公平である. A flat charge laid over a proportional one, falling hardest on those with least, inside an institution his title calls the source of mutual-aid thought. He does not reconcile the two.

NO OUTPUT TO MEMBERS. Not collective-good (nothing non-excludable is bought for the members, unlike averia_pool's armed escort), not indemnity, not a draw: receipts entered domain finances and 小林 finds no expectation of repayment — たとえ借上とはいっても実際には返済しないもの. PY1-PY3 left uncoded rather than propagated .NA, since .NA would assert a PY0 value not established.
大黒屋善兵衛 was 町方の商人 acting 藩の命をうけて — a townsman merchant convening on the domain's orders. 小林: 個人名を冠してはいるが、藩営頼母子、すなわち岩橋勝教授が称される領主的金融講であった. The personal name on the ledger conceals a domain instrument.

Nine meetings are recorded in the 銀集帳 between 嘉永元 (1848) and 嘉永6 (1853); 掛銀 falls across them from 700目 to 238目. Sources fail after the ninth, and a third association was begun the following year at 675目.

Nothing is priced ex ante in this association. NOTE A CONTRASTING DOMAIN, THOUGH: 小林 records that 高槻藩, from 文久2 (1862), ran a kō in which ある一定収支のモデル計算がなされていて、収益の多寡を判定して、それを藩財政に繰入している — an ex-ante model calculation of income and expenditure, profitability judged before commitment, at 25,000 shares. That is calculation inside a 領主的金融講 and would code differently.

Closed to the village: roughly 100 participants drawn from 高持 and 無高 households of 長興寺村. 無高 approached 40 per cent of the membership, and the 無高下 share of them fell from 41 per cent at the first meeting to 22 per cent at the ninth.

Enforceable through domain authority, which is what compulsory enrolment of a hundred households implies. Coded medium: no 議定 or 仕法書 survives, so the sanction is inferred from the fact of compulsion rather than read from a clause.
No peril is pooled. As with the other Japanese associations in this census, the arrangement moves capital rather than mitigating a hazard.

Rice contributions assembled into a large sum and drawn by one member at a time; no outsider bears anything. Confidence capped at medium because the source is a series of land-sale deeds (井本家文書), not a 仕法 — 三浦 never states the mechanism, he reconstructs the association from its wreckage.

Source silent on the ground of membership. 三浦 names the 親 (井ノ本左近) and ten 衆中 but says explicitly of 小磯二郎左衛門 and 西ノ左近 that it is 明らかでない whether they joined later or were non-members who took the pot — so the boundary of the association is not recoverable, let alone its basis.
Follows MB1. A named ten-member founding list would suggest restriction, but 三浦's own doubt about two participants means closure cannot be asserted from this source.
Not addressed.
懸足 falling due by round, the standard 頼母子 pattern 三浦 glosses from 下学集 as 出少銭取多銭. Medium rather than high: the periodicity is generic to the form, not stated for this association.

NOT INFERRED FROM THE NAME. The association is called 二石頼母子, which names a sum, not a contribution rule; the figures in 三浦's table (2石, 2石8斗, 3石, 田20代) are the LAND SALES by which members exited, not their 懸足. The rule is unrecorded.

Enforceable, and the evidence is the enforcement rather than a clause: over nine years members successively sold 先祖相伝の地 to the 衆中 and dropped out. 三浦's general finding is that the kō 絶えず田地を質として要求している and that membership required land yielding enough 得分 to cover the 懸足. Articulation .NR — no rule text survives for this association.
No hazard analysed; the source's question is landholding and lordship, not peril.
One member takes the assembled sum per round.
Entitlement is position in the cycle; no loss is claimed or verified.

DO NOT READ 落札 AS AUCTION HERE. 三浦 uses 落札 throughout, but his own note says 講親は初回に落札するのが慣例であるから、井ノ本左近は弘治元年に落札したものと思われる — the 親 took round one by customary right, not by bid. The term therefore cannot carry an auction reading, and the rule for later rounds is unrecorded.
Exposed well beyond contributions: default reached patrimonial land. 三浦: この場合頼母子は親たる井ノ本左近にとっては田地兼併の挺子となり、他の衆中にとっては先祖相伝の地を失なう契機となった. The obligation was not extinguished by what had been paid in.
Inapplicable: PY1 is rotation, so no loss is claimed and there is nothing to verify. Propagated .NA per CONTRIBUTING §4.
A 親-led association, but the locus of decision over the fund is not described. Consistent with every other kō row in this census.
Nine years of documented rounds (弘治元年 to 永禄六年 in 三浦's table). Whether it reached 満会 or collapsed as members were stripped out is not stated — which is itself the point of the case.
Applicable (DR1 is not open-ended) but unrecorded.

STILL .NR, AND DELIBERATELY SO AFTER THE VALUE SET WAS WIDENED. 'real-estate' would now fit, but 三浦's 頼母子講維持策として絶えず田地を質として要求している is a general finding about medieval kō, not an attestation for this association; what survives for Yamakuni is the series of land SALES by which members exited (782), which is default running its course, not a recorded pledge clause. Extending a vocabulary does not license filling a cell the source never fills.
Observed absence. Nothing in the association prices a peril ex ante; what the arrangement transfers is land, through default, not a distribution over outcomes.

Thirteen 口 at 1貫目 each assembled and drawn by one member; no outsider. Medium, and see adjudications: what is mutualised here is LIQUIDITY for commercial use, not a peril. 加藤's whole point is that this kō performed a 商業資金調達機能 against the received image of 庶民金融.

The 連名帳 establishes WHO joined (thirteen 口, mostly 御手洗町 merchants, two from 賀茂郡風早村 and 佐伯郡廿日市町 at 15 and 50 km) and that entry could run through a member's 取次. It does not establish the ground of eligibility. Prosopography is not a membership rule.
Numerically restricted and stated in the association's own 仕法書: 銀高拾三貫目無尽銀一口分掛銀一貫目宛持寄 — thirteen shares of one 貫目. The 連名帳 lists them by name.
Merchants subscribing on their own account; some recruited by a member's 取次. No compulsion anywhere in the record.
一会日之儀者、毎年六月十七日ニ相究銀子持寄仕可申事 — a fixed annual meeting day at which the silver is brought.

Equal per 口: 掛銀一貫目 before drawing, 掛戻銀一貫五百目 after. Note the rate is STATE-DEPENDENT rather than two-part — it changes on winning, it does not stack. This is a different structure from ko_daikokuya_1848's 高割+家割 and should not be conflated with it.

The 仕法書 as 加藤 quotes it carries no sanction for non-payment. By contrast the 天保11年 繁栄持寄講 of the same town does have 支払いが遅れた場合の措置 — so the silence here is a real gap in this document, not a general feature.
No hazard analysed.
毎年六月十七日に竹原屋平三郎宅で鬮取りがおこなわれ — one member draws the pot each year.
Entitlement is position in the cycle; nothing is indemnified.

鬮取り, and the discount is NOT bid: 掛銀 and 掛戻銀 are fixed at 1貫目 and 1貫500目 throughout. Order random, price fixed. The same town's 寛政11年「入札頼母子定法書並連名帳」 and 天保11年 繁栄持寄講 allocate by 入札 — see adjudications on the within-town contrast.

Capped independently of any loss: the draw is set by schedule at 13貫目 in year one rising 500匁 a year to 19貫目 in the last. Articulation .NR — the schedule is reconstructed from the ledger, not stated as a cap.

御連中之内、不時ニ銀子御入用之儀有之候節者、銘々之掛戻銀算用致預リ置、其余相渡し可申事 — on a member's sudden need his accumulated 掛戻銀 is reckoned and the remainder paid out to him. Confidence medium because the clause grants access to reckoned contributions rather than to a residual on winding up; whether that satisfies LS2's 'surplus' is the maintainer's call.

Exposed beyond contribution once he draws: the winner 質物書入 real property under 手形 with the town officials' 裏印. Note the exposure is STATE-DEPENDENT — it attaches on winning, not on membership. First form in the census where LS3 turns on a member's position in the cycle.
Inapplicable: rotation trigger. Propagated .NA.

竹原屋平三郎 hosts and 引請事支配 the 会席 and is also 町年寄 and the first winner, while the 所御役人中 countersign pledges. None of collective / elder-fixed / external-administered names a member-convener who is simultaneously a town officer. Coded .NR; consistent with every other kō row.
Thirteen numbered rounds (一番 … 十三番) in the 連名帳, one per year.
The association terminates when the thirteenth 口 has drawn; no perpetual fund is contemplated.

鬮当リ之節者、当所連中之内慥成質物書入ニて、所御役人中之裏印を取、手形相渡銀子預り置 — on drawing, the winner mortgages sound property by 書入, countersigned 裏印 by the town officers, against a 手形. 竹原屋平三郎 pledged 表口16間、裏行き22間の屋敷と2棟の蔵およびその付属の建物. Real property, publicly registered. Recoded from .NR when the value set was widened; this is the cell that first separates one kō from another in the census, against ko_usui_bango_1822 RB3=none.

Observed absence, and instructive. The association prices CREDIT precisely — a fixed 500目 premium on 1貫目, which 加藤 computes as a ~6% return, the highest of his three Mitarai cases. No peril enters the calculation. Same finding as the 中井家 ledger: calculation and peril-pricing come apart.
Eighteen 口 at 1000匁 assembled and drawn; no outsider. Medium, with the same caveat as the 1773 form — this is commercial capital, and about a third of the members are rice merchants pledging stock.
加藤 reconstructs occupations (7 of ~20 members are 米商人) but states no eligibility rule. Occupation is a property of who joined, not a ground of membership.
Eighteen 口 fixed in 「銀頼母子帳」 (表5-4).
Merchant subscription; no compulsion in the record.
Annual rounds on the pattern of the town's other associations. Medium: the 会日 clause is quoted for the 1773 無尽 and the 1840 講, not for this one.
掛銀 1000匁 per 口.

Compellable, and the clause explains why a pledge alone was thought insufficient: 万一懸戻し銀不埒ニ相成候節者、右質所売払候迄も、所ニゟ急ニ埒明不申方角も可有之候間、屹度請合人相立、是ゟ別紙受合証文差出、若懸戻し銀不埒之時者、右請合人ゟ相究可申事. Foreclosure was slow in some jurisdictions, so a 請合人 with a separate 受合証文 was made mandatory.
No hazard analysed.
取主 receives the assembled silver.
Position in the cycle; nothing indemnified.
The allocation clause is not among those 加藤 quotes from 「銀頼母子帳」. Do not infer 入札 from the town's other associations — that is precisely the inference the 1773 lot-allocated case forbids.
Exposed beyond contribution on two fronts at once: the 取主 files a 質物書入証文 AND a 請合人 gives a separate 受合証文, both deposited with 三笠屋藤三郎. Property and surety in the same instrument.
Inapplicable: rotation trigger. Propagated .NA.
The 御手洗御役人衆中 verify pledges by jurisdiction and 三笠屋藤三郎 holds the deeds, but decision-making over the fund is not described.
Runs until every 口 has drawn.
Applicable but unrecorded.

Property AND surety together, and the rulebook says why. 取主ゟ質物書入証文差出し候儀、勿論ニ候得共、万一懸戻し銀不埒ニ相成候節者、右質所売払候迄も、所ニゟ急ニ埒明不申方角も可有之候間、屹度請合人相立、是ゟ別紙受合証文差出 — the mortgage deed is taken for granted, but because foreclosure could not be effected quickly in some jurisdictions a 請合人 with a separate 受合証文 is made mandatory. The 質所 itself spans real property and goods: rice in store at 2000俵 (小原屋武七), 500-700俵 (three members), 100-200俵 (three more), with verification zoned by place (御手洗並尾道大小斎島質所者御手洗御役人衆中ゟ御見届被下候事; 津倉質所者今治ゟ). CAUTION FOR THE MAINTAINER: 'mixed' here is carrying two different mixtures at once — several kinds of property, and property plus surety. If that distinction ever matters, this row is the evidence for splitting it.

Observed absence. 加藤 computes a 1-2% return on this association against ~6% for the 1773 無尽, and notes that with 安永 and 天保 inflation these were not attractive as investments — the benefit was 一時に多額の資金を調達できるメリット. Credit is priced and compared; no peril is.
Thirty-four 前 at 1分 assembled for the 親; 松永: 親が「内證不如意ニ付」それを救済するために結ばれた頼母子である. Mutualisation among members with no outsider.

NO FITTING VALUE RATHER THAN SILENCE. 松永's general account of the 親頼母子 is that the convener 親類知人などから講員を集め — kin AND acquaintance, recruited by the person in need. MB1 admits kinship or contract, not a value that is both and neither. The specific 極証文 names 34 subscribers of 朴木沢新田 without stating a basis.
惣人数三拾四人持寄金 — the number of 前 is fixed in the 極証文 itself.
Subscribers are drawn in by request; no compulsion.
一人一会一分掛で年二会、三四会一八年で満会 — semi-annual contributions over thirty-four rounds.
1分 per 前, the 親 holding one 前 himself. State-dependent thereafter: those who have drawn pay 返金 of 1分 per meeting instead.
The 極証文 as quoted carries no sanction. 松永 discusses 順番変更 by consent and 礼金 elsewhere in the region, but not enforcement in this document.
No hazard analysed; the frame is 農業経営 and household liquidity.
鬮当人 receives the assembled 寄金.
Position in the cycle. The 親 takes round one entire — 初講は三四人が掛金を一分ずつ持ち寄り金額八両二分を親に与える — and thereafter the lot decides.

鬮 from round two, AND THE DISCOUNT IS FIXED NOT BID: 八両二分から四分の一を刎金（利息）として天引きして、残り六両一分二朱になるように. Order random, price fixed by rule — the exact inverse of the bidding kō, and the configuration in which 並松's regressive transfer cannot arise. See adjudications.
Capped independently of loss: 8両2分 gross, 6両1分2朱 net of the fixed 刎金, irrespective of the drawer's circumstances.

Members who have not drawn by round 29 stop contributing (二九会以後は、まだ鬮に当っていない人は、掛金を出さずに寄金を引取る), which is a schedule concession rather than a claim on a surplus. Nothing in the document establishes a residual claim.

The 極証文 does not address pursuit beyond contribution. 松永's other Echigo cases DO — 天明4年 梅沢村 儀左衛門 was sued with arrears of 32-33両 against a 書入田地 of only 80束刈 — but those are different associations and must not be imported into this row.
Inapplicable: rotation trigger. Propagated .NA.

三四会一八年で満会 — thirty-four rounds to completion over eighteen years.
Terminates at 満会; no continuing fund.

STILL .NR AFTER THE VALUE SET WAS WIDENED. The 極証文 records no security for this association. 松永's wider Echigo material would license positive values for OTHER associations — 書入田地 for the landed, and 親方・地主の保証 for the 小作農 長蔵 of 頸城郡中山村 who had no land to pledge, which is the first candidate to take RB3=surety — but those are different kō and must not be imported here. The 嘉永5年 case (右は今後の自分鬮当金を引当としている) is not an RB3 fact at all: the pool is the collateral there, not the creditor.

Observed absence. The 刎金 is a fixed one-quarter discount — credit priced by rule — and 松永 reads the last drawer's position as a 長期安定定期預金 yielding 8両2分 on 2両2分3朱銀1.29匁 of contributions. No peril is priced anywhere.

NO FITTING VALUE: NO PERIL IS AT ISSUE. Allocation, spreading and pooling all presuppose a peril being moved among parties with a stake. Nothing perilous is moved here: donors give land, the estate is let, rents fund a ritual banquet and the surplus is divided. Assets are pooled; no hazard is. Second form, with ko_daikokuya_1848, whose MC1 is unsettable specifically because no peril is at issue. COUNT CORRECTED 2026-08-12: an earlier version of this note said 'the fifth time' / 'the five forms'. That was wrong and the error was mine. MC1 is .NR on FOUR forms and only TWO of them — ko_daikokuya_1848 and shenhui_gu_alloc — are .NR because no peril is at issue. particular_average is .NR as the census's declared NULL CASE, where a peril exists and is deliberately not moved; warichi_iwade is .NR because a historiographical dispute is being held open. Those are three different reasons and they must not be summed.

Membership is constituted around a deity cult — in one instance a God of the Land and Grain association (土穀神會) in Shanyin county, Shanxi. Medium: the founding documents do not survive and Zelin infers the original basis from later sale contracts. Note the strain — by the time these contracts were written, shares had passed to buyers with no devotional relation to the cult, so 'confession' names the association's origin rather than the holders' qualification.
Whether the number of shares was capped is not recorded; the founding arrangements are lost.
Original entry was by donation 'commensurate with their largesse'; later entry was by purchase. Neither is compelled.

A single endowment of land or assets at entry, not a periodic subscription — which distinguishes this sharply from every kō in the census and from the tontines. Compare tontine_en_1693, the only other ex-ante-lump form.
Shares were received 'commensurate with their largesse' — the share IS the measure of the contribution.
No sanction for non-payment is recorded, and with a lump endowment there is nothing recurring to enforce.
No hazard is analysed; the source's question is property in shares.

The estate's primary output is non-excludable among members: rents fund banquets honouring the deity, with the items to be prepared itemised in some contracts, and the shareholders partook of them once the ritual was over. This is the averia_pool configuration — a fund that buys something for all members rather than paying any one of them.
Inapplicable where PY0 is collective-good. Propagated .NA per the vocabulary's applicability rule.
Inapplicable where PY0 is collective-good. Propagated .NA.
Inapplicable where PY0 is collective-good. Propagated .NA.

AN UNAMBIGUOUS RESIDUAL CLAIM, ARTICULATED IN THE CONTRACTS: 'if there was a surplus after the ritual functions of the association were performed, the remaining income from rents would be distributed among the shareholders.' Third form in the census to take LS2=1 after ko_usui_bango_1822 and ko_mitarai_mujin_1773, and the only one where the residual is a claim on a standing endowment rather than on a subscription cycle.
Whether a member could be pursued beyond his endowment is not addressed.
Inapplicable: no loss is ever claimed, so there is nothing to verify. Ninth consecutive .NA on VF1 in the East Asian material.
Who administered the estate and decided the ritual expenditure is not recorded; the surviving documents are share sales, not constitutions.
A standing endowment supporting recurring annual ritual, with shares passing by inheritance and sale across generations. Second open-ended form in the census.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA per the vocabulary's applicability rule.
No advance is secured; there is nothing for a pledge to attach to. Left .NR rather than none because the source does not address security at all.

Observed absence. Shares are priced — bought and sold like land, some conditionally — but nothing prices a peril, because no peril is borne. The same finding as the 中井家 ledger and the kō: calculation and peril-pricing come apart.

Members pay a fixed annual sum into a fund from which members are relieved; no outsider bears anything and nothing is paid to a third party. THE CENSUS'S CLEANEST POOLING CASE: unlike the forms whose MC1 cannot be set, a genuine peril — incapacity to work through illness — is mutualised across a membership. Note the fund is SEGREGATED: Masure describes the boxes as institutions under the guild but with 'aparte boekhouding en bestuur', separate accounting and management, and says establishing one was a way to 'de ambachtskas verlichten', to relieve the guild chest. That is asset partition inside a corporate body, and it is the same structural move as the no-set-off clause in the 御手洗 銀頼母子.

Membership is of 'leden van het eigen ambacht' — members of the craft itself — and the guild held an economic monopoly within its city, so the box is bounded by trade and by town together. First occupation-based form in the census; every kō is kinship, locality, contract or territorial-subject.

CLOSED BUT NOT CAPPED, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE SOURCE'S OWN. Masure states explicitly that the boxes had no numerical limit on membership and contrasts them with the guild almshouses, which did — twelve to sixteen widows for the Mechelen skinners, twenty smiths in Antwerp. Coded 1 because entry is closed by qualification (guild member of that craft in that city), not because numbers were restricted. Every kō in the census takes MB2=1 for the other reason, so this cell now conflates two things and may need splitting.

VALUE CHANGES WITHIN THE FORM'S PERIOD, RECORDED NOT SMOOTHED. Masure: many boxes began voluntary and became 'verplicht' for masters over the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Coded for the mature form at medium. If this matters comparatively it should be split on the tontine / ortoq / kabu precedent rather than hedged with P — the maintainer's call.

A 'vast jaarlijks bedrag', fixed annual amount, paid in advance of any claim. The thirteenth-century Sint-Elooisbroederschap shows an earlier variant: members kept a box in the workshop and paid in a proportion of turnover, one denier on transactions above ten schellingen.

A flat annual sum, but equal WITHIN a benefit class rather than across the membership. In some Brussels guilds a master's wife could pay a higher fee to qualify for the full master-level benefit instead of the three-quarters rate. Contribution and entitlement move together in tiers, which CN2's three values cannot express — third form after ko_daikokuya_1848 and the Mitarai kō where this has bitten.

Enforceable through forfeiture of entitlement rather than through distraint: a master's widow kept her right to benefit only 'as long as she continued to pay the annual membership fee and did not remarry outside the guild'. Masure records no legal sanction for arrears beyond loss of access and of full membership standing.

Not addressed. Sickness incapacity is idiosyncratic on any reading, but Masure never asks about correlation across members and the coding may not supply it. THIS IS THE CELL van Leeuwen 2012 SHOULD FILL — that study is reported to treat correlated risk and moral hazard directly, which would make it the first substantive HZ1 outside the maritime forms.

A named member is compensated for a realised misfortune. Only the third individual-indemnity form in the census, after general_average and widows_fund_scotland, and the first that is neither maritime nor actuarial.

THE ROW THIS FORM WAS ACQUIRED FOR. Payment is triggered by 'werkonbekwaamheid door ziekte', incapacity for work through illness, and it is an entitlement rather than a discretionary grant. The Brussels smiths' ordinance of 1473 states it flatly: 'Datter yemant inde voirs. bruederscap wesende zieck is, hij sij arm oft rijke, alle weke huer ziecte broot dragen oft sinden zelen moeten' — whoever in the said brotherhood is sick, be he poor or rich, must have his sickness bread brought or sent every week. Second realised-loss trigger in the census after general_average.
Determined by the trigger: the sick member is paid, there is no allocation among competing claimants.

CAPPED INDEPENDENTLY OF THE LOSS, AND GRADED BY STATUS RATHER THAN BY NEED. A master drew one to two masons' daily wages per week of illness in the fifteenth century; a master's wife about three-quarters of that, 'because her labour was valued lower'; journeymen, where admitted, three-quarters — Mechelen furniture makers in the early seventeenth century. The sum tracks the claimant's rank in the trade, not the severity of what befell him.

VF1 TAKES A SUBSTANTIVE VALUE FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THE EAST ASIAN AND MEDITERRANEAN MATERIAL ALIKE — it was .NA on nine consecutive forms. Procedure: the sick member notified the busmeester, who made a huisbezoek, a home visit, to establish the claim and paid the weekly sum on the spot. Guild tokens (gildepenningen) evidenced membership, not the loss. CONFIDENCE MEDIUM BECAUSE THE VALUE MAY NOT FIT: the busmeester is an officer OF THE FUND, elected from among the masters and accountable to the ambachtsdekens, not a public authority, and 'official-adjudication' may have been written for the latter. It is not communal-attestation — no fellow member swears — and not documentary. SPLIT MADE 2026-08-13: this characteristic now names the MODE only and the object is coded at VF2. The repair was a split, NOT the fourth state proposed in earlier drafts of this note — see logbook 4 for why a fourth state would have entrenched the conflation rather than removing it.

What happened when the box could not meet demand is not recorded. Masure notes no instance of a box running out and no emergency assessment on members, but does not treat the question, so this is silence and not an observed absence.
Whether members held any claim on the fund's surplus is not addressed; the surviving evidence is ordinances and benefit rates rather than dissolution accounts.
Whether a member could be pursued beyond his annual fee is not addressed. Nothing suggests it, but the source does not ask, so .NR rather than 0.

Two busmeesters chosen from among the masters, rendering account to the guild deans. In the fifteenth-century Brussels new shoemakers' box journeymen held equal voting rights in appointing the box administration. First collective governance in the census outside averia_pool and bazacle_mill, and the first in a membership relief fund.
A standing institution with its own accounts, running across the whole 1250-1600 span, not a cycle that completes. Third open-ended form after shenhui_gu_alloc and the levy funds.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA per the vocabulary's applicability rule.
No advance is made and nothing is secured; the source does not address security at all.

OBSERVED ABSENCE, AND THE GRADING IS THE EVIDENCE. Benefits are differentiated — master, master's wife, journeyman — but by RANK IN THE TRADE, not by any assessment of who is likelier to fall sick. Contributions are a flat annual sum. Nothing prices the peril ex ante. Same finding as the kō and the 中井家 ledger: an institution can grade, calculate and tier without pricing a hazard.

MEDIUM, AND THE HEDGE IS SUBSTANTIVE: THE POOL IS PARTLY FUNDED BY OUTSIDERS. Harris's 'pooling' requires mutualisation among stakeholders with no outsider, and these funds fail that in two documented ways. A sick or aged member could have a stand-in (noodhulp) appointed who did his work for half the pay, the other half going to the member — in 1750 the Amsterdam peat-porters drew a quarter of all fund income from substitutes, men who might remain substitutes with substitute rights until the end of their working lives. And city authorities granted guilds levies on third parties: the shipwrights taxed wharf owners and mast-makers, the peat-porters taxed every incoming peat ship, the Utrecht carpenters taxed incoming wood. At the guilds' zenith, members of the rich Amsterdam guilds 'probably paid no more than half of their welfare costs from their members' contributions, and sometimes considerably less.' A pool that transfers from non-members to members is not what MC1=pooling was written to describe. COUNT CORRECTED 2026-08-12: an earlier version of this note called this 'the sixth form in a row' to strain MC1. That summed three different problems. The strains are of distinct kinds — no peril at issue (ko_daikokuya_1848, shenhui_gu_alloc), a declared null case (particular_average), a dispute held open (warichi_iwade), and outsider funding (here). Only the first pair is a candidate for a vocabulary repair. STRENGTHENED 2026-08-13 ON AUDIT: THE SOURCE IS BLUNTER THAN THIS NOTE WAS. Van Leeuwen 2012, 76 on the noodhulpen - a sick member could have a stand-in appointed who did the work for half pay, the other half going to the sick member, and in 1750 the Amsterdam peat-porters guild took 'no less than a quarter of all its income from substitutes'. The substitute 'could remain a substitute member with substitute rights until the end of his working life'. Van Leeuwen's own verdict: the guild 'took full advantage of its position as official organizer of labour in a corporative political economy TO EXPLOIT NON-MEMBERS TO THE ADVANTAGE OF ITS OWN COFFERS', and at p.78 that this 'extended ... to the outright exploitation of substitutes to finance middle-class welfare'. Add the civic levies: the shipwrights taxing wharf owners and mast-makers, the peat-porters taxing every incoming peat ship, the Utrecht carpenters taxing incoming wood. At the guilds' zenith members 'probably paid no more than half of their welfare costs from their members' contributions, and sometimes considerably less'. SO FOR THE RICH AMSTERDAM GUILDS THE MAJORITY OF WELFARE COST WAS BORNE BY PEOPLE WHO COULD NOT CLAIM. Also note a funding structure this census has now seen twice: the Amsterdam surgeons stated in 1748 that 'benefits are paid from the interest on capital', which is the avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme structure inside a contributory guild box.

Of 225 sickness schemes surveyed in 1811, 150 were operated by guilds and 20 more by organisations of fellow craftsmen — 'this ensured a close link between occupation and insurance'. Only 46 were general schemes open to all.

Restricted on several margins at once, and every one of them is an adverse-selection control: maximum age on joining (30-32 for the Amsterdam shipwrights, 40 for the Beurs der Leydsche Gerechtigheyd, 50 for the Utrecht journeymen carpenters, 60 for the peat-porters); minimum membership periods before benefit; and explicit caps on the number of recipients — the peat-porters' old age scheme admitted a maximum of 45 pensioners.

COMPULSION IS THE MECHANISM, NOT AN INCIDENT OF IT, AND van Leeuwen SAYS SO. 'The city authorities sanctioned compulsory guild membership … and if there was a guild insurance fund this normally also implied compulsory membership of the fund. That allowed the guilds to circumvent problems of risk selection.' The counter-evidence is in the same table: the three non-guild associations he tabulates are all voluntary. And the natural experiment runs the right way — the Amsterdam carpenters made membership compulsory in 1708 because the fund would otherwise have been non-viable, relaxed it when the guilds were abolished, reinstated it in 1806 'financial necessity required', and went bankrupt in 1845 once compulsion became illegal. The census's fifth compulsory form, and the only one where compulsion is shown to be load-bearing. CONFIDENCE CUT FROM high 2026-08-13 ON AUDIT. Van Leeuwen 2012, table 9 makes compulsory membership a property of SOME schemes and not others: yes for the Amsterdam surgeons, shipwrights and peat-porters and the Utrecht master carpenters; NO for the Utrecht journeymen carpenters association, the Leiden journeymen woolcombers and the Beurs der Leydsche Gerechtigheyd. The cut appears to fall between masters' guilds and journeymen's bodies, and this row smears it. SPLIT CANDIDATE on the tontine_en/tontine_fr precedent, and it bears directly on the standing question of why four - now eight - forms are compulsory, since a masters/journeymen split would change that count. [verify]

An initial fee plus an annual premium: 150-250 guilders and 5 a year for the Amsterdam surgeons, 56-77 and 7-12 for the shipwrights, 10 and 4 for the peat-porters, 69 and 2 for the Utrecht master carpenters.

Flat within a class, but the classes are not flat against each other and one of them is risk-graded. Utrecht journeymen carpenters 'paid double the annual premium of their masters, though not the initial high fee'. More strikingly, a voluntary Haarlem burial fund admitted anyone in good health aged between twelve and forty and then demanded 'three guilders for each year that aforesaid person is over the age of forty' — an age loading, i.e. a contribution differentiated by risk. van Leeuwen presents that as an adverse-selection remedy, and it is the first risk-graded contribution anywhere in this census. CN2's three values cannot express it.

Arrears bar relief outright: assistance was denied if the applicant 'was behind in paying his premiums'. Kampen's journeymen went further — a member found feigning illness lost benefit for a year while remaining obliged to contribute.

THE FIRST SUBSTANTIVE HZ1 OUTSIDE THE MARITIME FORMS. Ordinary sickness is idiosyncratic; epidemic disease is not, and the funds knew it. The Amsterdam carpenters ruled that a brother taken ill 'from the rapid sickness of pestilence, red measles, and suchlike' be confined to his house for six weeks, drawing benefit throughout — a covariate shock provided for by rule. The flexing mechanism in LS1 exists precisely to absorb aggregate demand: 'If the number of sick members was too high relative to the available reserves, contributions might be raised, or a limit set on the number of sick given relief.' Coded mixed rather than idiosyncratic because both regimes are documented; medium because van Leeuwen never classifies the correlation himself.

A CONFLATION IN HZ2, EXPOSED BY THE FIRST NON-MARITIME CASE. The characteristic asks whether the hazard responds to the defence mounted against it, glossing 1 as adversarial (an enemy fleet) and 0 as indifferent (a storm). Illness itself is indifferent. But its CLAIMED incidence is not: 'Insurance against loss of wages when ill … might increase the frequency of reported illnesses', and in 1705 the Dordrecht shipwrights complained of brethren who collected sickness money and 'immediately or not later than the following day … repaired once again to the street, without being inconvenienced by any sickness'. The guilds answered with waiting periods of about a week for sickness and six months to a year for burial, doctors' certificates, and home checks. That is endogenous CLAIMING, not an adversarial hazard, and HZ2 currently has no way to distinguish the two. Coded P to record the strain; the maintainer may prefer 0 with the moral hazard recorded elsewhere.
A named member is compensated for a realised misfortune — sickness, old age, widowhood — in cash, at a rate between a third and a half of wages and two to three times poor relief.

Loss of earnings through illness, with burial, old age and widowhood as further defined events. Not discretionary: the Amsterdam carpenters' widows claimed a pension in 1770 'regardless of whether they were poor', the city authorities agreed, and the guild had to pay a widow holding shares worth 20,000 guilders.
Determined by the trigger; no allocation among competing claimants except through the rationing recorded at LS1.

CORRECTED 2026-08-13 FROM 1/high, ON AUDIT OF VAN LEEUWEN, AND THE SOURCE SAYS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT I CODED. A weekly rate is scheduled - table 9 gives 2 to 3.25 guilders around 1750 - but it is not a ceiling that holds. Van Leeuwen 2012, 78 documents the Leeuwarden bricklayers paying 100 guilders to a single recipient, 80 each to two, 60 each to three, and 40 per person beyond that, so THE INDIVIDUAL ALLOWANCE FALLS AS CLAIMANTS RISE; a Leiden widows' fund ruled in 1738 that beyond eleven or twelve widows 'the widows will have to be content with receiving as much less as there shall be more widows'; and 'if money was tight, guild administrators would not hesitate to cut allowances'. Duration is equally soft - table 9 shows a maximum of 26 to 32 weeks in three of seven schemes and none in four, while p.68 records benefit continued 'longer than the rules and regulations permitted' and 'restricted when the guild's resources were low'. P is right: a cap exists nominally and is not honoured under stress. SECOND P ON PY3, with friendly_society_female_england. Note the two are different shapes - there the schedule tapers by DURATION, here the allowance is divided by CLAIMANT COUNT.

A THIRD VALUE FOR VF1, AND THE FACET NOW DISCRIMINATES. 'Guilds almost invariably demanded a doctor's certificate, and often sent out someone to check on claimants at home.' Coded documentary because the certificate is the near-universal requirement and the home check the frequent supplement; guild_box_brabant takes official-adjudication for the converse case, where a visiting officer establishes the claim and no certificate is mentioned. CAUTION: the two run together here and VF1 permits only one value, so this coding suppresses the visitation. SPLIT MADE 2026-08-13: this characteristic now names the MODE only and the object is coded at VF2. The repair was a split, NOT the fourth state proposed in earlier drafts of this note — see logbook 4 for why a fourth state would have entrenched the conflation rather than removing it.

THE CENSUS'S CLEAREST LS1, AND ONLY THE FIFTH FORM TO CARRY ONE. Shortfall is shared by scaling every allowance down as claimants multiply. The Leeuwarden bricklayers' and masons' schedule of c.1750 sets it out in a table: one master alone draws 100 guilders, one master with one widow 80 each, three masters with five widows 45 and 40 respectively, and beyond that 40 per person. A Leiden widows' fund of 1738 states the principle outright — 'if it should happen that there are more than 11 or 12 widows and the fund has no surplus from previous years, in such case, but not otherwise, the widows will have to be content with receiving as much less as there shall be more widows.' van Leeuwen: 'If money was tight, guild administrators would not hesitate to cut allowances, tighten eligibility criteria, or refuse new applicants.'

Guilds accumulated substantial reserves — the Amsterdam surgeons held 94,000 guilders in bonds in 1800, some 450 per surgeon, and 223 of 770 Dutch guilds held bonds in 1798 — but whether members had any claim on that capital is not addressed.

Half-present as a structural fact. No member is pursued personally for the fund's debts, but the fund could raise the standing contribution on continuing members to meet demand — 'If the number of sick members was too high relative to the available reserves, contributions might be raised'. Exposure beyond the agreed contribution therefore exists, but it operates prospectively on the membership rather than retrospectively on the individual.

Administered by the guild's own officers — 'the fund's administrators' grant pensions, and 'guild administrators' cut allowances and tighten criteria — within a guild constitution. van Leeuwen does not describe how they were chosen, so medium.
Standing funds of great age: in 1811 the average age of a guild fund was 112 years, and 45 per cent of sickness schemes then extant were more than a century old.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA per the vocabulary's applicability rule.
No advance is made and nothing is secured; the source does not address security.

AN OBSERVED ABSENCE ON THE AUTHOR'S OWN TESTIMONY, WHICH IS RARE. van Leeuwen asks the question directly and answers it: premiums 'were generally not calculated in an actuarially sound way', and he argues this is 'insufficient ground to deny guilds the status of insurance companies'. The contrast case is in the same article — the Monnickendam widows' fund of 1754 charged age-related contributions when it 'was actuarially possible at the time to calculate sound premiums', set them too low anyway, and went bankrupt. So the technique existed and the guilds did not use it. Compare widows_fund_scotland PR1=1 and tontine_fr_royal PR1=P. CONFIDENCE CUT FROM high 2026-08-13 ON AUDIT, FOR CONSISTENCY WITH THIS FORM'S OWN CN2 NOTE. Van Leeuwen 2012, 76 introduces the Haarlem case under the heading 'Differentiation in contribution level by risk category is another way to counter adverse selection ... This happened on occasion' - free entry between 12 and 40, and above 40 'three guilders for each year that aforesaid person is over the age of forty years'. That IS a premium graded against a mortality gradient. It sits in a VOLUNTARY BURIAL FUND rather than a guild box, which is why 0 is retained, but the boundary between the two is doing real work in this cell and the source treats them as one system. Van Leeuwen's own summary at p.79 is that premiums 'were generally not calculated in an actuarially sound way', and at p.71 that an actuarially sound premium 'would have been so much higher as to dissuade most artisans' - the Monnickendam widows' fund, which did grade contributions by age, went bankrupt.

Relief flows from the gild's goods to its own members and no outsider bears anything, but the funding is largely ENDOWMENT rather than subscription: McRee calculates that a single member on the typical 8d. weekly stipend would consume 'nearly a fifth of the property income of a typical charitable gild' over a year. Coded pooling at medium because the mutualisation runs through corporate property rather than through pooled contributions — a different strain on MC1 from guild_box_dutch, where the fund was partly financed by levies on non-members. SECOND SOURCE, AND IT PULLS THE OTHER WAY. Goddard and Smalley 2024 on the Guild of St George, Nottingham, 1459-1546 — a different guild of the same class, read 2026-08-13 — find that membership payments 'represented between 78 and 82 per cent of the guild's annual income' in the 1470s and 80s, on an annual fee of 13d. So English religious guilds could be predominantly SUBSCRIPTION-funded, not endowment-funded, and the note above overstates the endowment reading. McRee's phrase is about property income as a denominator, not as the whole. The tension is left standing rather than resolved: two guilds, two periods, and the income mix evidently varied. It strengthens rather than weakens MC1=pooling. Goddard and Smalley contain NO discussion of relief to members and cannot be used for any other cell of this form.

THE CELL THAT SEPARATES THIS FORM FROM BOTH GUILD BOXES. These are religious fraternities, not craft bodies: 'lay associations of men and women' devoted to religious and social ends which 'drew their members from a variety of professions and made no attempts at industrial regulation'. guild_box_brabant and guild_box_dutch both take MB1=occupation. Membership here crosses trades, neighbourhoods and social groups, and McRee's argument is that relief provisions existed partly to bind that diversity into 'a strong collective identity'.

Whether entry was closed or capped is not addressed. McRee calls them voluntary associations of great popularity, which suggests open entry, but he never states a restriction and the returns he uses would not necessarily record one.

'a type of voluntary association that enjoyed tremendous popularity during the late Middle Ages'. Contrast guild_box_brabant and guild_box_dutch, both compulsory in their mature forms — and in the Dutch case compulsion is shown to be what made the fund viable.

Not established. McRee says charitable provisions 'required members to pledge their willingness to contribute, either individually or corporately', which leaves open whether that meant regular subscription or assessment as need arose, and the 1388-89 returns he works from record promises rather than payment schedules.
Follows CN1. No contribution basis is recorded.
Not addressed.

Not analysed, though the peril list is the widest in the census and mixes the two kinds freely: leprosy, blindness, paralysis, being struck dumb, loss of an arm, leg, foot or eye; robbery, fire, shipwreck, storm damage, flood; old age; wrongful imprisonment; and in nearly every case 'a catchall category to cover acts of God'. Correlation across members is never asked about.

A weekly cash stipend to a named member — 3d. at Lincoln's Gild of Saint George, 14d. typically in London, an average of just under 8d. across the twenty-three fraternities that stated a figure. Some paid in kind instead or as well: the Gild of Saint George the Martyr at Great Yarmouth issued a cloak, hood, hose, shoes and linen annually.

THE FINDING, AND IT FALSIFIES A RESULT. guild_box_brabant and guild_box_dutch both take PY1=realised-loss, and on fifteen comparable cells they differed from each other on one. This form separates from both here. The occasion is a realised misfortune but the entitlement is not: 'Gilds did not offer to replace valuables that had been lost or destroyed, but only to help members with living expenses when such losses had reduced them to penury.' The Ludlow Palmers' Gild return of 1388-89 makes the assessment two-sided and caps its repetition — relief 'once, twice, and thrice, but not a fourth time, as much help shall be given to them, out of the goods of the gild, as the rector and stewards, having regard to the deserts of each, and to the means of the gild, shall order'. Wallis's reported claim that English craft provision was discretionary rather than organised insurance is confirmed here for the religious gilds, from the returns.

Where the trigger does not fix the sum, officers do: the Beverley Gild of the Purification set a range and left 'the final determination to the discretion of the alderman and seneschals', who 'could award anywhere from 4d. to 8d. per week, depending on the circumstances surrounding each case'.

HALF-PRESENT AS A STRUCTURAL FACT. 'Most gilds specified a fixed allowance', which is a cap independent of the loss; but Beverley's officers varied the award case by case, which is not. A third kind of cap operates on frequency rather than amount — Ludlow's 'once, twice, and thrice, but not a fourth time'. PY3 cannot hold a frequency cap at all.

INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION OF THE DUTCH VALUE FROM A THIRD TRADITION, WHICH MAKES pro-rata THE CENSUS'S BEST-ATTESTED LS1. The Wisbech Gild of Saint John the Baptist 'warned that it would pay needy members the promised weekly stipend only as long as gild funds lasted', and the Gild of the Holy Trinity, Saint Mary and All Saints at Roughton stipulated that if more than one member required help the weekly grant of 1d. 'would have to be divided among all those in need'.
Whether members held any claim on gild property is not addressed.
Not addressed. Relief comes out of gild goods and nothing suggests recourse against members' estates, but the question is not asked.

A THIRD FORM ON THIS CELL, AND IT EXPOSES A WELL-FORMEDNESS PROBLEM RATHER THAN A MISSING VALUE. Officers adjudicate — 'the rector and stewards, having regard to the deserts of each'. But WHAT IS ADJUDICATED IS FAULT, NOT THE FACT OF THE LOSS. Stratford-on-Avon's Holy Cross Gild relieved poverty that was 'undeserved'; the Gild of Saint Mary in Cambridge denied aid to anyone impoverished 'si non per latrocinium meretricium seu aliam viam malignam'; another refused members guilty of rape or adultery; a London gild cut off any member caught begging in the city. McRee: 'gild mercy was not undiscriminating … the indigent were not all equally worthy of gild favor.' So guild_box_brabant establishes the loss by visitation, guild_box_dutch documents it by certificate, and this form adjudicates blame — three different OBJECTS of verification under one characteristic that names only MODES. VF1 is asking two questions at once, in Sereno's sense, and should be split rather than extended. SPLIT MADE 2026-08-13: this characteristic now names the MODE only and the object is coded at VF2. The repair was a split, NOT the fourth state proposed in earlier drafts of this note — see logbook 4 for why a fourth state would have entrenched the conflation rather than removing it.

NO FITTING VALUE. Decisions rest with named officers — rector and stewards at Ludlow, alderman and seneschals at Beverley — which is neither a collective assembly, nor a founder's fixed instruction, nor external administration. GV1's three values are written for other shapes of body. Coded .NR rather than forced; third form where GV1 could not be set.
Standing fraternities with property endowments and no terminal horizon.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA per the vocabulary's applicability rule.

Mostly inapplicable, since relief was a stipend and not an advance — but a minority of gilds lent instead, and for those nothing secured the loan. Kingston-on-Hull's Gild of the Blessed Virgin Mary 'promised to lend 10s. to any man or single woman who had fallen into poverty', asked repayment within three years and 'offered to forgive the debt if the borrower proved unable to repay'; the Gild of Saint Lawrence in Lincoln lent but barred further funds to anyone who had failed to repay. Coded .NR rather than none because the lending gilds are a sub-practice and may warrant their own form.

Observed absence. Stipends are set by custom, wealth and locality — 3d. at Lincoln, 14d. in London 'undoubtedly reflecting the capital's wealth and higher cost of living' — and nothing anywhere prices a peril or grades a contribution against one.

The incorporation relieves its own poor from corporate funds raised on its own members — a 1583 decreet arbitral prescribed contributions to a 'common purse', and an 'Act of stent for the poor of the craft' levied on craftsmen, over which Calderwood records 'a stirre among the crafts' who 'murmured' at the collection. Medium: the fund is corporate rather than subscribed, so as with guild_relief_england the mutualisation runs through the body's own resources.

The incorporation of Mary's Chapel, Edinburgh — ten distinct building arts incorporated under one title, whose members called themselves 'the House'. Third occupation-based form after the two guild boxes.

Relief is for freemen of the incorporation and their dependants; Charles Brown's route is the standard one — apprenticed, then burgess and guild brother in June 1678, then freeman of the incorporation in November. Closed by qualification rather than numerically capped.

Contribution to the poor of the craft was levied by act of stent on the craftsmen, not subscribed voluntarily, and incorporation membership was itself required to practise the trade in the burgh. Medium — Allen documents the levy and the resistance to it but does not treat compulsion as a design question.
Standing contributions to the common purse and periodic stents, in advance of any particular claim.
How the stent was apportioned among craftsmen is not stated. Allen's evidence is the disbursement side — pension lists and discharged accounts — rather than the assessment side.
Not established, though the recorded 'stirre' and 'murmur' over the collection imply enforcement was contested.
Not addressed. The perils relieved are old age, bodily infirmity and widowhood; correlation across members is never asked about.

Quarterly cash to a named person. Margaret Smibert was enrolled in 1728 at £4 Scots quarterly, later raised to £5 and then £6; the Michaelmas pensions of 1727 ran from £4 to £8 quarterly. Distinguished in the records from 'supply', one-off payments meeting immediate need — the relict of Thomas Henry received both on 11 January 1670.

SECOND need-assessed FORM, AFTER guild_relief_england, AND THE PETITION IS QUOTED IN FULL. Margaret Smibert petitioned in 1728 'Representing that by reasen of old age and infirmitie of bodie she was altogether disabled to subsist her selfe and there by reduced to extream want and poverty', whereupon 'The incorporation takeing her circumstances to their seriouse Consideration Appointed her to be enrolled as one of their pensioners for Foure pounds Scots money quarterly … AND TO CONTINOW DURING THEIR PLEASURE'. Allen: before the widows' fund the safety net 'was wholly discretionary'.

Amount as well as eligibility is determined case by case on petition, and status enters the determination: Allen cites Aberdeen rates where a guild brother's pension was £120, a craft pension £50, a guild widow's £27 and the common poor's £9, and Stewart's finding that some received 'money commensurate with their social status not their actual level of need'.

A fixed quarterly sum unrelated to the size of any loss, and explicitly capped — Allen notes of the 1761 reform debate that 'both pensions and supply were capped'. Medium because the sum was revisable upward at the incorporation's pleasure, as Smibert's was twice.

THE OBJECT OF VERIFICATION IS NEED, NOT THE FACT OF A LOSS AND NOT FAULT — A THIRD OBJECT. The incorporation in assembly took the petitioner's 'circumstances to their seriouse Consideration' and enrolled her. Compare guild_box_brabant (a visiting officer establishes the fact of incapacity), guild_box_dutch (a certificate documents it) and guild_relief_england (officers adjudicate desert and blame). This is a second form verifying something other than the fact of the loss, which partly meets the falsification condition set in logbook 4 — but not the specific condition stated there, which was a second form verifying FAULT. Recorded, not acted on. SPLIT MADE 2026-08-13: this characteristic now names the MODE only and the object is coded at VF2. The repair was a split, NOT the fourth state proposed in earlier drafts of this note — see logbook 4 for why a fourth state would have entrenched the conflation rather than removing it.
Capping is recorded but no sharing rule is. What happened when demand exceeded the box is not described, and the 1761 motion to abolish supply payments in favour of larger pensions 'was not adopted'.

OBSERVED ABSENCE, AND IT IS THE HINGE OF THE PAIR. A pension ran 'during their pleasure' — revocable at will, with no claim on the incorporation's funds. craft_widows_fund_edinburgh reverses this to LS2=1, and that reversal is what the 1768 scheme was for.
Not addressed.

The incorporation decides on petition and the boxmaster disburses — Katherine was admitted 'In amongst the ordinary pensioners att Candilmes nixt' before 'the boxmaster was ordered to give her ane Rex dollar In supplie'.
A standing corporate obligation; Allen's accounts run continuously from 1674 to 1782 and the incorporation's minutes begin in 1553.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA.
No advance is made and nothing is secured.

Observed absence, and the grading is the evidence: awards track rank — guild brother, craftsman, guild widow, common poor at £120, £50, £27 and £9 in the Aberdeen comparison Allen cites — not any assessment of who is likelier to fall into need.

Subscribers' quarterly contributions, plus contributions from the incorporation's own funds and from the deacons, accumulate into a capital of £5,500 sterling from which annuities are paid to subscribers' widows. No outsider bears anything.
Members of the incorporation of Mary's Chapel. The scheme sits inside the craft body and is not open beyond it.

Subscribers only, and entry is time-barred: the first annuities were payable only to widows of contributors who died after Martinmas 1774, six years after adoption, because the capital was not yet raised. Interim widows fell back on the discretionary pensions of craft_pension_edinburgh.

THE REVERSAL FROM craft_pension_edinburgh. Capital came from the incorporation's funds, from the deacons, and 'from the individual members who OPTED INTO the scheme'. The scheme was itself adopted by vote — forty-three to thirteen on 8 March 1768.
Quarterly contributions from subscribers over six years to build the target capital, alongside investment of the fund 'upon proper security, bearing interest'.

Whether subscriptions were flat or graded by age is not stated. This matters: an age-graded contribution would be the first true risk-differentiated premium in the census, and Webster's involvement makes it possible, but Allen does not say.
Not addressed.
Not addressed. Mortality across a single craft in one burgh is idiosyncratic in ordinary years and covariate in epidemic ones, but Allen does not raise the question.
An annuity to the named widow of a deceased subscriber.

The trigger is the subscriber's death, not any assessment of the widow's circumstances — 'a fairer system which paid out to ALL contributors'. That is the whole point of the reform, and it is what separates this row from craft_pension_edinburgh PY1=need-assessed. Joins the tontines and the priced life annuity as a life-event form.

NO FITTING VALUE. Once the capital was raised 'the widows were to receive an equally divided portion of its annual produce'. Equal division of a fund's income among all eligible claimants is not rotation, auction, indemnity or need-assessment, and PY2 has no state for it. Recorded rather than forced.

NOT CAPPED, AND THAT IS THE STRUCTURE. The annuity is 'an equally divided portion of [the capital's] annual produce', so it floats with the fund's income and the number of widows rather than being fixed. The interim rate was £10 sterling only because the capital was still being raised. Contrast craft_pension_edinburgh PY3=1, a fixed quarterly sum.

There is no unmet loss to distribute because the entitlement IS a share of the fund's produce — shortfall is absorbed automatically by the size of each portion. Second form in the census on this value, and the only one where it is the scheme's design rather than a fallback.

THE HINGE. Subscribers' widows hold a claim on the fund's annual produce as of right. craft_pension_edinburgh has LS2=0 — a pension granted 'during their pleasure'. One institution, two regimes, opposite values, and Allen's argument is that the 1768 scheme existed precisely to convert the one into the other.
Whether subscribers could be called on beyond their contributions is not addressed.
Not described. With a life-event trigger there is little to verify beyond the fact of death and of subscription, and Allen does not record how either was established.

Adopted by ballot of the membership — 'passed by forty-three votes to thirteen' on 8 March 1768, after printed details were circulated by Balfour & Smellie 'for the members to consider before voting on its adoption'.
A standing annuity fund built on permanent invested capital.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA.
No advance is made to members. The fund's own capital was invested 'upon proper security, bearing interest', but that is the fund as lender, not as borrower, and RB3 asks about the latter.

HALF-PRESENT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS WORTH THE CELL. Actuarial expertise is directly present: the scheme was built with Dr Alexander Webster, an architect of the 1744 Scottish ministers' fund which Hare and Scott call the first actuarially-based fund in the world, and Allen calls the response 'decidedly actuarial'. But the mechanism Allen describes is capital accumulation against a £5,500 target with the produce divided equally — a savings pool, not a premium priced against a survival function — and he nowhere says contributions were graded by age. So expertise attaches to the DESIGN PROCESS and not demonstrably to the INSTRUMENT. Compare widows_fund_scotland PR1=1, which rests on an unverified citation and should be checked against Hare and Scott 1992 before either cell is relied on.
Lodge members contribute and lodge members are relieved; 'local clubs managed their own funds, elected officers, and ran their own affairs'. No outsider bears anything.

The lodge is the unit and it is local — the Stanhope Agricultural Oddfellows Lodge in Durham, the Hartlepool Star of Temperance, the Halifax Crown Lodge. Membership crosses trades within a locality: Prom's lodges hold 'miners, artisans, and agricultural laborers' together. Not occupation, which distinguishes this from the guild forms.

AGE-CAPPED ENTRY, AND THE CAP HAS TEETH: 'the standard admissions policies of nearly every friendly society banned new members after that age [forty]'. Prom's point is the consequence — expulsion after forty 'essentially left members … unable to secure any sickness insurance or medical care for the rest of their lives'. An adverse-selection control whose bite is measured in the impossibility of re-entry.
Subscription to a lodge; no compulsion.
Regular contributions in advance of claim; Prom's evidence is members falling 'weeks behind in their payments'.
Contribution rates are not given. Prom's sources are lodge minute and fines books, which record discipline rather than tariffs.

HALF-PRESENT, AND THE GAP BETWEEN NORM AND PRACTICE IS THE DATUM. The rule was enforceable and the practice was not: 'Although national leaders tended to discourage the practice, members were usually granted sick pay and medical attendance even if they had fallen weeks behind in their payments.' Contrast guild_box_dutch CN3=1, where arrears barred relief outright, and guild_box_brabant CN3=1, where the widow's entitlement lapsed with her fee. First form in the census where a contribution rule is documented as systematically unenforced.
Not addressed; Prom's subject is discipline and charity rather than the actuarial structure.

Same reading as guild_box_dutch and the same strain on the characteristic. The illness is indifferent; the CLAIM responds to the insurance, which is why lodges banned 'drinking, being outdoors, or working while receiving sick pay' and sent a visitor to 'investigate suspected fraud'. George Wardle was fined £6 — a de facto expulsion — 'after he falsified his eligibility for sick pay and medical attendance'. HZ2 still cannot distinguish endogenous claiming from an adversarial hazard.
Sick pay and medical attendance to the individual member; a surgeon was contracted for in-home visits and simple medicines, with complicated procedures excluded.
Incapacity through sickness. Fourth realised-loss form, with general_average and the two guild boxes.
Determined by the trigger; no allocation among competing claimants.

A standing rate rather than a sum measured against the loss — the Durham Loyal Star of the North let a member keep 'one month's worth of sick pay (£2)', which implies a fixed weekly figure. Medium: Prom quotes no schedule.

FIRST USE OF communal-attestation IN THE CENSUS, AND THE ROW THAT SETTLES THE VF1 QUESTION. The verifier is a fellow member, not an officer and not a document: the sick visitor is 'the fellow member sent round to offer moral support for the ill member, or to investigate suspected fraud'. NOTE WHAT HE VERIFIES — BOTH the condition AND the claimant's conduct, since lodges banned drinking, being outdoors and working while on the box. So within ONE form the mode is communal and the object is dual, while guild_box_brabant pairs an official mode with a condition object, guild_relief_england an official mode with a fault object, and craft_pension_edinburgh an official mode with a need object. Mode and object vary independently across four forms and jointly within this one. That is the discriminant-validity evidence Campbell & Fiske require and it was absent when the split was declined on 2026-08-12; see logbook 4. ENFORCEMENT WAS ALSO LAX, WHICH IS ITS OWN FINDING: visitors 'turned a blind eye', Benjamin Goodwin warned members when he would be coming round, and officers ignored district demands to stop payment.
