Insolvency and the distribution of shortfall are not treated.

Not addressed as a claim, though Prom records surplus funds being voted to charitable purposes — the Royal Rutland Lodge at Scarborough and the Hartlepool Star of Temperance both applied surpluses by resolution of the membership, which implies the surplus was the lodge's to dispose of rather than the members'.
Not addressed.

'Most societies were organized on a lodge system, whereby local clubs managed their own funds, elected officers, and ran their own affairs.' Discipline is exercised by the assembled lodge — fines and expulsions are minuted, and Prom's evidence base is the fines books.
Standing lodges federated into orders and districts.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA.
No advance is made to members; security is not at issue.

Observed absence in this source. The only risk instrument Prom records is the blunt admissions bar at forty, which is a selection rule and not a price; no premium is graded against any distribution. Note that the actuarial literature on these societies exists and is not used here — Broten on their financial viability is in the collection and would test this cell.

The busmeester's huisbezoek establishes THAT THE MEMBER IS INCAPACITATED and nothing else — Masure records no inquiry into how the incapacity arose and no conduct condition attached to drawing. Object and mode are independent here: the same object is established documentarily in guild_box_dutch.

CORRECTED 2026-08-13 FROM loss-occurrence/high, ON AUDIT OF VAN LEEUWEN. The certificate establishes incapacity, but it is not the only thing established, and van Leeuwen 2012, 68 lists the grounds of refusal outright: assistance was denied if the applicant 'had not been a member long enough, or if he had been sick too long or too often, was behind in paying his premiums, HAD INCIDENTAL EARNINGS THAT RESCUED HIM FROM POVERTY, or if he led an unseemly life - if, for example, he had an illness (such as venereal disease) or injury (perhaps incurred in a fight or through being drunk) ATTRIBUTABLE TO REPREHENSIBLE CONDUCT'. That is claimant-fault and claimant-need and conduct-compliance alongside loss-occurrence. Van Leeuwen 2012, 76 adds that rules voiding benefit where the insurer 'had been wilfully misled' were 'part and parcel of the rules of guild funds', with guild boxes at Groningen, Haarlem and The Hague refusing claims where the applicant was already ill at admission, understated his age, or concealed an illness. FOURTH mixed FORM - the falsification condition recorded on 2026-08-13 for splitting VF2 into a ternary per object is now MET.

Need — McRee: gilds helped 'only … when such losses had reduced them to penury'. And fault — Stratford-on-Avon relieved poverty that was 'undeserved'; Cambridge St Mary denied aid to anyone impoverished 'si non per latrocinium meretricium seu aliam viam malignam'. The fact of the misfortune is not itself what is established.

The petition represents circumstances and the incorporation weighs them: Margaret Smibert was 'by reasen of old age and infirmitie of bodie … altogether disabled to subsist her selfe and there by reduced to extream want and poverty', and the incorporation took 'her circumstances to their seriouse Consideration'. Need, not the occurrence of a defined event and not fault — which is what makes this form the third distinct object under one mode.

THE ROW THAT FORCED THE SPLIT. The sick visitor goes 'to offer moral support for the ill member, OR to investigate suspected fraud' — condition and conduct in one office. Lodges banned 'drinking, being outdoors, or working while receiving sick pay', so what is policed while relief runs is compliance, not merely the illness. A communal mode carrying a dual object, which is the within-form separation of mode from object that Campbell & Fiske require.

Members subscribe and members are relieved, but a class of contributors takes nothing back. A Stafford roster of 1797 lists 65 HONORARY against 111 subscribing members; York's rules divide the society into 'Two Classes, viz. Honorary Members' and 'General Members', the honorary paying six shillings a year for a seat on the governing committee while being 'exempt from fines and received no benefits'. Contributors who cannot claim are outside Harris's pooling as written — the second mechanism by which that has happened, after the noodhulpen and civic levies of guild_box_dutch. The boundary was permeable: a Burton-on-Trent honorary member 'reduced in circumstances' became entitled to the same relief as the 'inferior sisterhood'.

Parish-based for the most part — St Mary Redcliff, St Augustine, both Bristol parishes. A few were occupational, such as the Female Friendly Bookbinders, but Rusnock and Dietz report that most rules did not restrict by trade; where occupations are named it is to EXCLUDE, as in the society barring any woman 'that gets her living in the streets'.

THE TIGHTEST ENTRY SCREEN IN THE CENSUS, AND IT SCREENS ON HEALTH AS WELL AS AGE. Only women 'free of any distemper or sickly constitution', in a 'good state of Health', with 'no bodily disorder or weakness' could join; 'No lame, no infirm, would be admitted'; one set of rules required that a candidate must already have had the smallpox. Concealing an illness to gain admission was 'immediate grounds for exclusion'. Age: typically capped at forty, some at thirty, minimum usually sixteen, with some societies instructing members to enrol their unmarried daughters by that age and one fining those who failed to.
Subscription to a club; no compulsion.
Regular subscriptions plus entrance money, with fines levied on top — members needed 'cash to pay regular subscription fees (and the fines and additional charges)'.

FLAT WITHIN THE BENEFIT-BEARING CLASS AND NOT OTHERWISE, WITH TWO DEPARTURES THAT CN2 CANNOT HOLD. First, the two-class structure: honorary members paid a separate annual contribution — six shillings at York — for governance rights and no benefits. Second, and more consequentially, the ENTRANCE FEE WAS GRADED BY AGE: societies 'proved wary of registering the elderly' and 'a few groups took much older women, but only in exchange for higher entrance fees'. That is a contribution differentiated by risk, the second instance in the census after the Haarlem burial fund in guild_box_dutch. Confidence low because Rusnock and Dietz quote no schedule of rates.
Stewardesses were responsible for 'levying and collecting fines', and the disciplinary range ran to 'warnings, fines, suspension of benefits' and expulsion.
Not addressed; the article's subject is the definition of sickness and work rather than the actuarial structure.

Same conflation as guild_box_dutch and friendly_society_england, but here the control is unusually explicit. Societies 'prohibited members from working while on sick pay', and in Bristol's First Female Protectant Providential Society, 'If one of the daily visitors found a sick member working, her relief would be terminated immediately and an official hearing convened.' The illness is indifferent; the claim is not. HZ2 still cannot separate endogenous claiming from an adversarial hazard.

Weekly cash to the sick member. Rates: five shillings a week at St Mary Redcliff for the first four weeks, 'a benefit that approximated prevailing wage rates'; seven shillings and sixpence in the larger Bristol society, with 'a possible total of almost fifty pounds for long illnesses'.

THE TRIGGER IS FUNCTIONAL, NOT MEDICAL, AND THE RULES SAY SO: 'to be sick meant to be unable to work: illness was defined in functional rather than medical terms.' The Bristol formula is 'sick or any way affected by the Hand of God, and unable to work'. Note what the definition then EXCLUDES: the Earl-Shilton society confined full benefit to members 'whose illness, in the common course of human events, must speedily terminate in recovery or death', while 'Blindness, habitual lameness, insanity' did not qualify because 'such conditions did not interrupt a normal working life, they precluded one'.
Determined by the trigger; no allocation among competing claimants.

THE CENSUS'S FIRST TAPERED BENEFIT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS P AND NOT 1. The sum is fixed against the loss but declines with its duration: St Mary Redcliff paid five shillings a week for four weeks and then two shillings 'until she recovered'; a Hampshire society three shillings for thirteen weeks and thereafter '1s. a week only, WHILE IT IS THOUGHT NECESSARY' — a flat cap in the first phase and a need test in the tail. St Augustine reduced after a month, capped the reduced relief at six months, and barred re-application for two months 'unless Seized with a Fever'. Permanent disability was handled separately: one society gave members who became blind half the weekly benefit for life. PY3's ternary cannot express a schedule that changes shape over the life of a claim.

SECOND communal-attestation FORM, AND THE VERIFIER IS A FELLOW MEMBER BY ROTATION. 'All societies depended on the work of stewardesses, who were responsible for visiting sick members and dispensing benefits'; an officer 'usually visited the sick member once or twice per week to verify her complaints and pay her benefits', daily in the largest Bristol society. Stewardesses came to office 'through either election or strict rotation', the latter 'most common, suggesting that the duties were to be distributed equitably', serving terms of three months to a year — so the verifier is any member in turn.

THIRD mixed, AND THE TWO OBJECTS ARE SEPARATELY EVIDENCED. Loss-occurrence: the visitor calls 'to verify her complaints'. Conduct-compliance: 'If one of the daily visitors found a sick member working, her relief would be terminated immediately and an official hearing convened.' One office, one visit, two things established — which is the pattern that forced the VF1/VF2 split and is now attested in a second tradition and a second period.

Insolvency and the distribution of shortfall are not treated, though the article notes that 'A society's material survival depended upon defining how and when to compensate members' — the tapering at PY3 is the cost control, and it operates before any shortfall arises.

Not addressed as a claim. Stewardesses did decide 'whether a portion of the fund could be lent with interest', which implies the fund was the society's to deploy rather than the members' to claim, but Rusnock and Dietz do not put it that way.
Not addressed.

'The self-governing societies thus were democratic, with each member serving as stewardess or on the committee at some point during her active membership.' Office by election or, more commonly, strict rotation; terms from three months to one year. In the two-class societies honorary members held committee seats alongside representatives elected from the general membership. Note the legal setting: these were bodies in which married women 'who had no independent standing in law' none the less voted, held office and administered funds.
Standing clubs; the article works from thirty-nine sets of rules written between 1780 and 1830.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA.

No advance is made to members. The society itself lent at interest — stewardesses determined 'whether a portion of the fund could be lent with interest' — but that is the fund as creditor, which RB3 does not ask about.

HALF-PRESENT, AND THIS IS THE CLEAREST EX-ANTE PERIL PRICING IN A MEMBERSHIP FUND SO FAR. Two screens operate at entry: health, excluding anyone with 'any distemper or sickly constitution' or 'bodily disorder or weakness', and age, capped at forty or thirty. Where the age bar was relaxed it was relaxed FOR A PRICE — older women were admitted 'only in exchange for higher entrance fees'. That is a charge graded against expected claim, without any mortality or morbidity table, which is exactly the reading given to tontine_fr_royal. Fourth P on PR1, and the first arising from a health screen rather than an age band alone.

CODED allocation RATHER THAN pooling, AND THE REASON IS THE CENSUS'S THIRD CONTRIBUTOR-BENEFICIARY DISJUNCTION. The capital is donated: 'hali vakti yerinde olanlar kazançlarından bir kısmını ... bağışlamışlardır' - the comfortably-off gave part of their earnings - and the intended beneficiaries are 'ödeme kabiliyeti olmayan kişiler', those without the ability to pay. Donor and beneficiary sets are disjoint IN ROLE but not in community, and the first draft of this note overstated the point. Kars 2020 is explicit that the founders relieve their OWN quarter - funds set up 'kendi mahalleleri halkını bu vergi yükünden kurtarmak için', to free the people of their own quarters from this tax burden, by 'aynı yerleşim birimi eşrafından maddi gücü yerinde olanlar', those of means among the notables of the same settlement unit. So this is the York honorary-member structure of friendly_society_female_england rather than the outsider funding of guild_box_dutch: contributors sit inside the community and outside the beneficiary class. Still the third case, and still the reason MC1 needs its companion, but the three are not the same shape. The exposed do not fund the fund, so nothing is pooled among them; a hazard is shifted onto an endowment. BUT SEE THE SPLIT CANDIDATE ON MB3: Küçük states that avarız funds were capitalised EITHER by wealthy donors OR as 'mahalle ve köy ahalisinin kendi aralarında oluşturdukları bir yardım sandığı', an aid fund the inhabitants formed among themselves. The second variant would take pooling. One type row cannot hold both and Kırkçeşme evidences only the first. [verify]

The mahalle, and the mahalle is defined in this literature by mutual answerability: a place of people 'birbirlerini tanıyan, aynı ünite içindeki davranışlarından dolayı birbirlerine karşı sorumlu olan ve ortak bir dayanışma duygusu içinde yer alan' - who know one another, are responsible to one another for their conduct within the same unit, and stand in a common feeling of solidarity. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY BETWEEN THE TWO FUNCTIONS: relief goes to the quarter, but credit did not stop there - 'mahalle sakinleri ile civarda yerleşik olan diğer ahalinin bu sandıktan kredi kullanmasına imkân tanınmaktadır', residents AND other people settled in the vicinity could borrow. MB1 records the relief boundary; the lending boundary is wider and the characteristic cannot say so.

Not addressed for the relief side; residence in the quarter appears to be the whole of it. What Küçük does record is a screen on the CREDIT side, and it is reported as a general norm rather than from the Kırkçeşme book: local merchants and artisans preferred, no credit to 'ticari sicili sorunlu' traders, and requests from the örf class - kadı, müderris, sipahi, yeniçeri - not permitted. THAT NORM IS CONTRADICTED BY THIS FUND'S OWN ACCOUNTS, where 'örfi yöneticiler' take some 15 per cent of the credit (Küçük 2025, 163). Norm-against-practice gap of the same shape as friendly_society_england CN3, and left .NR rather than coded because the screen governs borrowing, not membership. The Turkish is also ambiguous as to whether the örf exclusion governs borrowing or the choice of mütevelli. [verify]

Propagated .NA. There is no membership to join or decline: the fund is an endowment settled on the quarter, and residence in the quarter is what makes one a potential beneficiary. Compulsion attaches to the LEVY, not to the fund, and coding MB3=compulsory would import the tax's character into the institution that relieves it. Contrast averia_pool, where the levy IS the pool.

THE MOST INFORMATIVE CELL IN THE BATCH, AND IT IS THE warichi_iwade SIGNATURE. Nothing is collected from those exposed. The fund is capitalised once - 6,280 kuruş of anapara vakfedilen to the quarter - and thereafter lives on its return. Every other membership fund in this census assembles a stream: the 掛金 of the kō, the guild-box subscription, the friendly-society weekly, the tontine payment. This one does not, which is the structural reason MC1 sits at allocation. CN2, CN3 and LS2 propagate .NA.
Propagated .NA from CN1. No contribution stream to characterise.
Propagated .NA from CN1. No contribution to enforce.

MIXED, AND THE MIXTURE IS THE POINT. The perils enumerated for these funds run across both classes: covariate - 'deprem, sel, yangın gibi doğal afetler', earthquake, flood and fire, relieving the victims after the event - and idiosyncratic - the funeral costs of the poor, contributions to the marriages of orphaned and destitute children, and the tax share of the individual household that cannot pay. The fiscal obligation itself is covariate to the point of being perfectly correlated, since the levy is assessed on the quarter as a body; WHICH HOUSEHOLD FAILS to meet its share is idiosyncratic. First form in the census where a single fund holds both classes explicitly. Kars 2020 extends the covariate list for the class with SALGIN HASTALIK, epidemic disease, alongside fire, earthquake and flood, and adds the capital needs of those entering business ('iş hayatına atılanların sermaye ihtiyacına') to the idiosyncratic side. Epidemic is the census's first epidemiological peril.
Not addressed. Küçük discusses screening of borrowers but nothing on whether relief altered the conduct of those relieved.

LOW, AND THE LOW IS DOING REAL WORK: THIS FUND OUTPUTS BOTH AND PY0 ADMITS ONLY ONE. Individual-indemnity, which is why it is coded so: relief to victims of particular earthquakes, floods and fires; the funeral of a particular poor person; a marriage portion for particular orphaned children; the share of the particular household that cannot pay. Trigger and allocation at PY1 and PY2 rest on that same evidence and are specific. Collective-good, which is why the confidence is low: the upkeep, repair and staff costs of the ulu cami, medrese and imarethane come out of the same budget, and Küçük treats this as the clearest demonstration of the funds' role - 'mahallenin kolektif giderlerini karşılamada bu vakıfların rolünü en açık şekilde bize gösterir'. The Kırkçeşme disbursements are largely of that second kind: 47 kuruş to the Vakıf Nazırı, 150 to the mütevelli's salary, 272 to meet debts, 13.5 to accounting. P WOULD BE THE RIGHT SHAPE AND IS NOT AVAILABLE - it has never been used on a nominal characteristic in this census and PY0's allowed_values do not admit it. Recorded rather than forced; see logbook 4.

Relief follows the event: victims of earthquake, flood and fire have their needs met 'sonrası', afterwards; a death produces the funeral cost; an inability to pay produces the assumption of the share. Not rotation, not a life-event schedule, not a standing entitlement. Note that this is a WIDER peril list than any coded form except Gazzini's confraternities - natural disaster, death, destitution and fiscal incapacity in one instrument.

The abstract states the design directly: donations were made 'ödeme kabiliyeti olmayan kişilerin yararlanması amaçlanmıştır', intended for the benefit of persons without ability to pay. Beneficiaries are 'ihtiyaç sahipleri', those in need, and 'kimsesiz ve muhtaç' children. Need, not a rota and not a proportional entitlement. Medium because Küçük quotes no rule fixing how need was established or ranked among competing claims.
No cap is stated. The operative constraint is upstream and absolute - see LS1 - since disbursement could not exceed the year's nema, but that budgets the fund rather than capping any claim.

THE HARDEST CAPITAL-LOCK-IN RULE IN THE CENSUS, AND IT IS STATED AS A PRINCIPLE. 'Para vakıflarında sarf işleminin kesinlikle elde edilen kâr üzerinden yapılması gerekmektedir. Ana paradan harcama yapılmaması esası benimsenmiştir.' Expenditure must absolutely be made out of the profit obtained; the principle that no expenditure be made from the principal was adopted. It is enforced by personal liability: even the officials collecting the avarız akçesi were to indemnify the fund if principal were spent. So the loss falls where the year's return runs out - capped at the nema, with the corpus untouchable. At Kırkçeşme that ceiling is 942 kuruş against 6,280 kuruş of principal, a hair over fifteen per cent. RESIDUAL RULE ADDED FROM KARS 2020, AND IT MAKES THIS A FIRST-LOSS LAYER RATHER THAN A SIMPLE CAP: 'gelirleri avarıza tahsis edilir, gelir yetmediği zaman verginin geri kalan kısmını mahalle halkı aralarında paylaşarak öderlerdi' - the income is allocated to the avarız, and WHEN THE INCOME DOES NOT SUFFICE THE PEOPLE OF THE QUARTER PAY THE REMAINDER BY SHARING IT AMONG THEMSELVES. So the fund's liability is capped at its annual nema and the excess reverts pro-rata to the households. LS1 can hold one of those and not the layering, and 'capped' is retained because it describes the fund, which is the unit coded - but the members are NOT capped, and reading this cell as though they were would invert the risk-bearing. Kars also confirms the untouchable corpus independently, from a different century: 'böylece ana kaynağa dokunulmamış olurdu'.
Propagated .NA from CN1. Nobody contributed and so nobody can claim a residue; the corpus is inalienable in any case under the rule at LS1.

Observed absence for beneficiaries, who owe nothing and can therefore be liable for nothing. Note the asymmetry the characteristic cannot express: liability beyond contribution DOES fall on the mütevelli and on collecting officials, who must make the fund good from their own property if principal is expended. The person exposed to loss beyond his stake is the administrator, not the beneficiary.

The kadı. 'Vakıftan borç verilirken işlemler mahalle kadısının gözetim ve denetimi altında gerçekleştirilmektedir' - lending from the waqf was carried out under the supervision and inspection of the quarter's kadı - and the fund's records were registered in the şer'iyye sicilleri, which is how Küçük can reconstruct the debtors at all. The mütevelli acts, the court supervises. Sixth official-adjudication form.

Deliberately not assumed, on the precedent set for averia_pool and general_average. The kadı's supervision is documented for the LENDING side - security taken, terms, registration - and Küçük says nothing about what was established before relief was granted. Whether the object was the fact of the disaster, the claimant's need, or his compliance is exactly the question VF2 exists to ask, and guessing it would waste the instrument. Kars 2020 on the Istanbul court records is the item most likely to settle it and is unread.

CORRECTED 2026-08-13 AFTER READING KARS 2020. Originally coded external-administered at HIGH on the reasoning that 'the beneficiaries do not choose him'. THAT WAS AN INFERENCE, NOT EVIDENCE - Küçük names the mütevelli (Yalcıoğlu Terzi Ali Ağa, salaried 150 kuruş against 47 to the Vakıf Nazırı) and gives the selection CRITERIA - 'Dürüstlüğü sabit olan ve ticari faaliyetler konusunda bilgi ve tecrübesi olan kişiler tercih edilmiştir', established honesty plus commercial experience - but nowhere says who does the selecting. Kars 2020 on the Istanbul funds of 1618-1697 says plainly that the administrators 'mahalleli tarafından seçilir ve yine mahalleli tarafından mahkemede tescil ettirilirdi', were chosen by the people of the quarter and registered by them at court, which is collective and is the opposite of what I wrote. Different fund and different century, so Kars cannot fill this cell; but it destroys the inference that filled it. Held .NR until a source states the selector for THIS fund. The kadı's power to replace a mütevelli whose betrayal is proven is oversight, not appointment, and does not settle GV1.
A waqf in perpetuity; the corpus is inalienable and the institution has no terminal date.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA.

FIRST OCCURRENCE OF surety IN THE CENSUS, AND IT ARRIVES PAIRED. Borrowers had to furnish 'rehn-i kavî ile kefil-i melî uygulamalarından birisi veya her ikisini birlikte' - one of, or both together, a strong pledge and a solvent guarantor - at the fifteen per cent 'onu on bir buçuk' rate under muamele-i şer'iyye. Küçük glosses the alternatives exactly: 'kıymetli bir rehin' able to cover the debt, or 'zengin bir kefil' who would pay in the debtor's place. mixed is right for a rule that admits either or both. THE WIDER DISTRIBUTION IS IN DENIZ 2026, on 97 sixteenth-century deeds: about half stipulate no security at all, roughly a quarter require pledge AND guarantor, about a fifth guarantor only, and four deeds pledge only; Özcan's transaction records give 18 per cent none, 62 per cent guarantor only, 7 per cent both, 11 per cent pledge only, so deeds and practice diverge. TWO CONSEQUENCES RECORDED SEPARATELY: the personal/none discriminability problem, and the legal suppression of real-estate pledges. See CHANGELOG and logbook 4. CONFIDENCE CUT FROM high TO low, SAME DAY, AFTER READING ÇINAR 2017 - AND THE REASON IS A SOURCE-CRITICAL POINT THAT BEARS ON EVERY RB3 CELL CODED FROM A CONSTITUTION. Çınar shows that 'rehn-i kavî veya kefîl-i melî ya da ikisinden biri' is not a description of practice but a DRAFTING FORMULA: it appears in almost every cash-waqf deed, 'klişeleşmiş ve bir formüle dönmüş', stereotyped and turned into a formula, and he omits examples of it from his study precisely because it is boilerplate. Küçük's wording for this fund is that formula verbatim. So what I coded at high was very possibly a clause copied by a scribe rather than security actually taken at Kastamonu. THIS ALSO EXPLAINS THE DENIZ/ÖZCAN DIVERGENCE recorded above - deeds and transaction records disagree because the deeds are formulaic and the transaction records are not. GENERAL RULE THIS ESTABLISHES: RB3 coded from a deed records drafting convention; RB3 coded from an account of actual advances records practice; the two must not be pooled. [verify against the Kırkçeşme muhasebe defteri's own loan entries]

Observed absence, and unusually well evidenced for a zero. The rate is fixed by law, not by the borrower's risk: ten per cent standard in waqf lending, fifteen per cent the legal ceiling, and Küçük notes that departures from the fifteen per cent margin were a matter requiring separate treatment. Kırkçeşme's 942 on 6,280 is fifteen per cent flat. Security is demanded of everyone alike rather than graded, and nothing is priced against any distribution of loss. A price ceiling is the opposite of a risk-graded premium. ÇINAR 2017 ADDS THE SELECTION SIDE, AND IT IS RISK-BASED WITHOUT BEING A PRICE. Founders stipulated that the money not be lent to janissaries, to kadıs, to travellers, to 'denizlerde dolaşanlara' - those who roam the seas - to the known unemployed, or to anyone connected with fraudulent dealings; nor outside the city, nor to residents of another city, nor for a term exceeding one year. Every one of those exclusions screens for absconding, unenforceability or volatility, which is peril management by categorical exclusion rather than by a graded charge. Same structure as friendly_society_england, where the only risk instrument is an admissions bar. Çınar also gives the motive for preferring muamele-i şer'iyye over mudarebe, müşareke and bidaa in the mütevellis' own terms - 'riske girmeme, güvensizlik ortamı, vakıf parayı zâyi etme', risk-avoidance, an environment of distrust, and fear of losing the waqf's money. Capital preservation, articulated, and it governs the instrument choice.

OBJECTION REGISTERED, NOT A HEDGE; confidence lowered from high 2026-08-17. The opgeld is a price paid for carrying the peril - 'mitsgaders noch 34 gelijcke gld. ten hondert tot opgelt ende voor 't aventuyr van der zee' (no. 948), in the same words in all 36 contracts - which is MC1=spreading as defined. But the arrangement is equally allocation as defined: bilateral, a named counterparty, no fund. THE TWO VALUES DO NOT EXCLUDE ONE ANOTHER, and this form satisfies both. Winkelman's Inleiding states the transfer - the borrower wishes 'het eigen risico te beperken en tot het bedrag van de lening over te dragen aan de uitlener' - while the outsider criterion fails inside the corpus: in nos 1993, 3236 and 3237 the lender is the freighter or charterer of the same ship. Coded spreading because the priced premium is the salient fact; the cell must not be read as excluding allocation. Independent instance of the non-partition queried on MC1's exemplar 2026-08-16 and recorded in logbook 1.

Perils named in the acts run from idiosyncratic to covariate. Storm and wreck ('verongelucken', nos 3231, 3232, 3240, 3242) fall on one ship. Seizure is fleet-wide: no. 956 names 'nemen, ranchioneren ende beschadigen van Duynkerckers oft andere zeerovers'; nos 3232, 3234, 3235 'rovers oft andere piraten'; nos 3240 and 3242 'nemen, blijven, houwen, kerven, werpen, ransoeneren, haverije grosse ende alle anderen periculen'. No. 3237 prices the closing of the Danzig pontcamer, a seasonal covariate event. Coded mixed because one figure prices both kinds.

The form spans both, as general_average's HZ2 does. Storm is indifferent to the defence mounted; privateers and pirates are not, and the corpus shows the defence being bought - the ship in no. 1995 is 'gemonteert zijnde met 6 gootelingen ende 4 steenstucken', and the protest at no. 1992 records part-owners disputing 'den coop van seeckere geschut' bought for the voyage without the common owners' knowledge. P is a structural half-presence, not a hedge: both hazard kinds sit inside the same priced clause.

Exposure beyond the pledged thing is expressly stipulated in eight of the 36 contracts - 'mitsgaders zijn persoon ende alle sijne goederen voorn. ende toecommende, egeene uitgesondert' (no. 952; likewise 951, 1991, 1993, 3229, 3232, 3234, 3239) - and no. 1991 adds three sureties bound 'als principaele' renouncing beneficium excussionis et ordinis. The protests act on it: nos 959 and 960 threaten recovery on 'die personen van den voorn. schipper ende sijn reders ende alle haere andere goederen'. MEDIUM not high: the remaining contracts name only the special pledge, which is .NR on the general question and NOT 0; and no. 1996 records a debtor denying general recourse on a cargo bodemerij - 'alsoo immers geen reeden is dat hij hem verder behoort te verbinden. Temeer dewijle de rogge hem alleen is verbonden bij de bodemerijebrieff.' STRAIN: LS3 is worded for a 'member' of a pool; this is a bilateral covenant.

Not recorded, and the silence is worth a row. In 46 acts - 36 contracts and 10 protests - no loss at sea is ever claimed, proved or adjudicated. All ten protests concern non-payment, non-acceptance or deviation, never a shipwreck. The verification machinery the corpus does show is documentary but establishes the wrong fact for this characteristic: the bodemerijbrief drawn in three identical originals with a separate advysbrief (no. 960), exhibition of the letter by the notary, formal insinuation at the debtor's house. How a lender's discharge on total loss was actually established cannot be read from this corpus and must not be inferred from the discharge clause.
Dependent on VF1, which is .NR rather than 'none', so this is .NR and not .NA: the corpus does not show that verification was absent, only that it is not recorded. See LM-0516.

Thirty of the 36 contracts run for one named voyage and end 'ter plaetse 't schip sijn rechte last sal commen te breecken, wel heynder maer niet verder te seylen' - the standing formula. Six do not: no. 962 runs a whole year with free navigation to Bremen, the Eider, Norway and the Baltic; nos 3229 and 3231 for three months and upward, the ship free to sail 'Oost, West, Suyden ende Noorden'; nos 1999, 2003 and 3239 run per month until repaid, no. 1999 expressly allowing early repayment with opgeld pro rata. Coded on the majority. The six time-based acts are a floating credit on the ship at sea-risk rather than a voyage bottomry; flagged in logbook 4 as a candidate form, not split here.
Principal and opgeld fall due together 8, 10, 12, 14 or 16 days after the ship's arrival, the interval named in each act. Nothing survives the voyage.

The money runs 'op 't recht aventuyr van der zee' in every act and the lender loses advance and opgeld together if the pledge is lost; Winkelman's Inleiding states it flatly - 'De geldgever verbeurt de lening en het opgeld als het onderpand verloren gaat.' THIS IS WHAT SEPARATES THE FORM FROM marine_insurance, where RB1 is third-party: here the peril-bearer has advanced the capital and his exposure is bounded by it, so the value of ship or cargo above the advance stays with the owner. MEDIUM not high: six acts push toward 'shared' - in nos 956, 3232, 3234, 3235, 3240 and 3242 the lender bears partial loss pro rata alongside the borrower, 'penninck ponts gelijck', and not only on total loss.

Market risk stays with the borrower: the opgeld is a fixed figure that does not move with the price the cargo fetches, and no act makes repayment conditional on a sale. WARNING ON THE LABEL: 'capital-provider' here denotes the BORROWER - owner of ship or goods - whereas at RB1 the same value denotes the LENDER. A secured loan has two capital providers, and RB1/RB2's role labels presuppose a single capital-labour axis, so the pair cannot be read off one another. Flagged in logbook 4 as a locator ambiguity in Sereno's sense; NOT repaired here and no characteristic added. Contrary evidence: at no. 1994 an acceptor offered to sell the pledged goods and pay over only the net proceeds 'sooverre 'tselve suyver provenu sal commen te strecken' - but he was protested against for it, so that was a refused accommodation, not the contract's term.

Every act names its pledge and the objects differ. The keel and gear, 'op kielscheeps ende 't gereetschap van dien', is commonest and is what the word bodemerij names. Fractional parts are pledged as such - 2/15, 3/16, 5/32, 5/8, a half, an eighth. Freight is pledged in its own right, and in nos 3236 and 3237 the lenders, who are also the charterers, may simply deduct principal and opgeld from the freight they owe. Goods and their returns are pledged in eleven acts. Eight add the borrower's person and whole estate present and future; no. 1991 adds three sureties. NOTHING IN THE DRAFTING marks ship-pledged and goods-pledged acts as different instruments - same two notaries, same registers, same clause architecture, same name - which bears directly on the bottomry/respondentia boundary; see logbook 4.

Discharge on total loss is carried by the standing formula in every act and named as the form's defining oddity in Winkelman's Inleiding: 'De geldgever verbeurt de lening en het opgeld als het onderpand verloren gaat. Dit is ongekend in het credietwezen.' Two acts define the risk period to the hour rather than relying on the formula: in no. 2000 'sal 't risicque ende pericule ingaen' only once the goods are loaded at Nykoping, 'alsdan eerst maer eerder niet', and it ends when the ship 'tot Lixbona in Portugael gearriveert sijnde, 't ancker 24 uyren geworpen sal hebben'; no. 1998 fixes inception at departure from Nykoping. QUALIFICATION: in six acts discharge is proportional rather than all-or-nothing - the lender shares partial loss pro rata and takes pro rata of net salvage, 'pro rato van 't suver gesalveerde' (nos 3231, 3232, 3234, 3235, 3240, 3242). NAMED 2026-08-18 on Rossi 2018, 91: THOSE SIX CLAUSES ARE AVERAGE, NOT ABANDONMENT. Rossi's pair is compensation for actual damage against transfer of the thing-at-risk for the full sum. Schuster makes abandonment the Bodmerei's default release - the debtor cedes the pledge and is discharged entirely - and the Amsterdam acts do the opposite, having the lender 'pro rato van 't suver gesalveerde ... mede genieten'. Taken with LS3=1 this is one pattern in two independent clauses: Amsterdam drafting converts an in-rem, all-or-nothing settlement into a personal, proportional one. NOT A CANDIDATE CHARACTERISTIC - average against abandonment is a settlement pattern, and the census adds forms, not features.

The strongest cell in this coding. All 36 contracts fix the price of the peril before departure and attach it in terms to the peril: 'tot opgelt ende voor 't pericule ende aventuyr van der zee'. The figure tracks route and duration - 5 1/8 per cent Konigsberg to Amsterdam (no. 3238), 7 to 12 per cent for single Baltic runs, 24 to 35 per cent for Iberian-plus-Baltic combinations; Winkelman reports 70 per cent for a Brazil destination elsewhere in the series. SIX ACTS CARRY A SCHEDULE of alternative rates keyed to alternative routes in the same instrument: 34 or 27 (no. 948), 35 or 25 (no. 950), 31 or 21 (no. 953), 10 or 18 (no. 954), 21 or 27 (no. 958), 17/17/9 (no. 2001). Five price by the month, 1 to 3 1/2 per cent (nos 1999, 2003, 3229, 3231, 3239). Where a route falls outside the contract the rate goes to arbitrators - 'tot seggen ende discretie van goede luyden hen dies verstaende' (nos 3227, 3237, 3241). WHAT IS NOT ARTICULATED, and PR1's coding rule turns on it: the opgeld is ONE figure covering interest and peril together and no act separates them. Winkelman's Inleiding does separate them - 'Het is rente voor de lening en een premie voor het risico' - and Verwer computes what is left 'na aftrek van desen voorraed tot Asseurantie', but both are inferences from outside the instrument. ANY PURE RISK PREMIUM EXTRACTED FROM THESE RATES IS analyst-imposed AND MUST BE CODED SO.

THE DECLARED DIFFERENTIA, coded 2026-08-17. Schuster states it as the form's defining feature: 'Die eigentliche Besonderheit der Bodmerei besteht darin, dass der Vertrag - im Gegensatz zum antiken Seedarlehen - lediglich eine auf das Pfand beschraenkte, dingliche Haftung des Schuldners begruendet; an das persoenliche Vermoegen des Reeders kann sich der Glaeubiger grundsaetzlich nicht halten. Es handelt sich also um einen Fall der Verpfaendung mit reiner Sachhaftung.' The operative mechanism is abandonment: n.17 has the debtor entitled 'sich durch Abtretung des Pfandes von jeder weiteren Haftung zu befreien', a right still in the ALR II 8 s.2427. MEDIUM, NOT HIGH, AND THE REASON MATTERS: 'grundsaetzlich', and n.17's proviso 'wenn nicht besondere vertragliche Vereinbarungen hinzutraten'. THE SHIELD IS A DEFAULT RULE, NOT A MANDATORY ONE. bodemerij_amsterdam LS3=1 is that default contracted out of as routine drafting - eight of 36 Amsterdam acts add an express charge on person and whole estate, one adds sureties renouncing beneficium excussionis, and the protests execute against persons and goods. The two rows therefore separate on a substantive value of this characteristic rather than contradicting each other, and the Marseille statutes 1253/55 already have personal liability arising only by special agreement. PAIRED WITH sea_loan.LS3=1 (LM-0526, 2026-08-17), which is Schuster's own contrast: the ancient sea loan binds the whole estate, the Bodmerei binds the pledge alone. The differentia is now testable and it separates - LS3 reads 1 / 0 / 1 across sea_loan, bottomry and bodemerij_amsterdam where RB4 reads 1 / 1 / 1. ABANDONMENT CORROBORATED 2026-08-18: Rossi 2018, 91 defines the early-modern pair - 'average', compensation for the actual damage, against 'abandonment', in which the party transfers ownership of the thing-at-risk in return for the full sum and so avoids 'the lengthy process of liquidation of damages'. That is the shape of Schuster's Abtretung des Pfandes. Rossi also explains why the mechanism is nearly invisible in the statutes, which matters for reading this cell: of the sixteenth-century compilations only the Burgos Ordinances of 1538 and 1572 and the Antwerp Compilatae of 1608 provide for abandonment expressly, while Florence, Genoa, Seville, Bilbao, the earlier Antwerp compilations and the by-laws of Amsterdam 1598 and Rotterdam 1604 are silent; the evidence sits in notarial declarations of abandonment.

source_ref: Schuster 2005, 112 and 120 (with n.526); 119-120 on the Exekutivklausel

The manager's peril exposure is at least a half and may be the whole, and the sources read do not settle which. Two mechanisms run together. (i) On the milveh half the capital is his and he owes it back as a debt, so peril loss on that half is his outright. (ii) On the pikkadon half he is a PAID bailee, not an unpaid one, because Maimonides requires the investor to pay him a wage or an extra share for his work; Ackerman-Lieberman 2011, 662 draws the consequence - 'unlike the ordinary agent, who, like any other unpaid bailee, is not held liable when an item is lost or stolen, the active partner in an 'isqa would actually be held liable in such circumstances'. MEDIUM AND ANALYST-IMPOSED, DELIBERATELY: the source addresses loss and theft, not maritime peril, and does not say whether the Talmudic ones exemption (unavoidable accident - shipwreck, brigandage) relieves the paid bailee here. Coded shared as the value the evidence supports; labour-provider would assert more than the source does. Resolving this needs Gamoran 2008 or Ackerman-Lieberman 2014, neither of which is held with a PDF. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION FROM OUTSIDE THE JEWISH-LAW LITERATURE: van Doosselaere 2009, 68, comparing the Genoese commenda with its eastern analogues - 'both the chreokoinonia and the ISQUA agreements suggest the idea of debt, or at least equal and joint liability, which severely restricted the pairing of participants with substantial differences in wealth... whereas in the western Mediterranean, any traveler could take a large amount invested by a wealthy investor on a sea venture because HIS LOSS WAS LIMITED TO THE VALUE OF HIS LABOR.' A Genoese economic sociologist, reading Pryor and Udovitch rather than the Talmud, arrives at the same allocation.

THE DISCRIMINATING CELL AGAINST commenda_alloc AND qirad_alloc, AND THE ONLY FORM IN THIS BATCH WHERE THE MARKET SIDE IS THE ARTICULATED ONE. Ackerman-Lieberman 2011, 663: 'because the structure of the Talmudic 'isqa allocates the active partner half of the invested capital as a loan, Maimonides holds the active partner responsible for HALF OF ALL TRADING LOSSES to the partnership capital. The corresponding relationship described by Islamic law - the investment partnership known as the commenda (qirad or mudaraba in Arabic) - holds the active partner indemnified from all partnership losses.' The two forms are set against each other on this exact question by the source itself. WHY THE ARTICULATION FLIPS: the Latin and Islamic sources name the peril (a voyage clause) and leave the market side to be inferred; the rabbinic source names the trading loss and leaves the peril to bailment law. The doctrinal pressure is different - ribbit forces the discussion onto the return on capital, the periculum clause and the hadith are about the voyage. DOCUMENTARY COUNTER-EVIDENCE THAT CUTS THE OTHER WAY, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT BEARS ON qirad_alloc RATHER THAN ON THIS ROW: at 664 Ackerman-Lieberman reports that 'legal documents from the Geniza concerning investment partnerships allocate both partners a share of both profits and losses, with very few documents indemnifying the active partner against losses'. On his reading those documents are 'isqa-shaped, which is his thesis; on Udovitch's and Goitein's they are qirad in practice, in which case qirad_alloc RB2=capital-provider is a doctrinal coding that the instruments contradict. The dispute is left open as a coding rather than resolved - see the type-row key_source and logbook 5.

POOLING, AND THIS IS THE DIFFERENTIA AGAINST avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme, WHICH IS allocation. Kars states the principle in general terms: 'her mahalle paylarına düşen avarız vergisi borcu için ortak bir bütçeyle avarız vakfı kurmaktaydı' - each quarter founded an avarız vakfı with a COMMON BUDGET for the avârız debt falling to its share - and 'Bu vakıflar mahalle halkının katkılarıyla kurulmuş ve çeşitli vesilelerle yapılan bağışlarla zenginleştirilmiştir', established with the CONTRIBUTIONS OF THE QUARTER'S PEOPLE and enriched by donations on various occasions. Gürsoy supplies the mechanism: 'Aynı mahallenin ihtiyaçları için birden fazla vakfedilmiş vakıflar avarız sandıklarında toplanarak gereken yerlerde kullanılmak için fon oluşturmuşlardır' - several waqfs endowed for the same quarter's needs were gathered into avarız sandıkları to form a fund. Contributors and beneficiaries are one set, the mahalle, and no outsider bears the hazard. MEDIUM NOT HIGH, AND THE RESERVATION IS REAL: Kars's Table II names individual vâkıfs and his conclusion calls them hayırsever (philanthropists), so the donor-endowed pattern of Kırkçeşme coexists in the same corpus. This row codes the aggregating chest; the single-endowment case is the other row. This is the SPLIT CANDIDATE avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme's key_source recorded as 'NOT YET EVIDENCED' - it is now evidenced.

The mahalle, and in one case the village. Gürsoy gives an articulated restriction: waqf 1735:26/101/47 was endowed to the avarız sandığı of Licana village, Ziştovi kaza, 'yalnız bu köyde oturan kişilere borç verilmesi şart koşulmuştur' - on condition that loans be made ONLY to persons resident in that village. LOCALITY AND NOT confession, AND THE EVIDENCE IS DIRECT: Kars's Table II records non-Muslims both endowing and borrowing - Meryem binti Devlet nam nasraniyye, Aleksan veledi Avanas, Mikail veledi Azar, Nikolas veledi Sadet, Simaven veledi Vartan - and a separate hane-i avarızı for the Armenian community of Bursa and the Ankara and Tanrıvermiş congregations. A confessional reading of the Ottoman quarter fund does not survive its own donor list.

Not addressed for the relief side; residence in the quarter appears to be the whole of it, and no numerical closure is stated. What the sources give is a screen on the CREDIT side - Gürsoy's Licana condition restricting loans to village residents, and Kars's borrower lists - which is the same asymmetry avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme MB2 records and is coded the same way for the same reason. Coding 1 from a lending condition would answer a question about membership with evidence about credit.

VOLUNTARY, AND THIS IS THE CELL WHERE THIS ROW LEAVES avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme's .NA BEHIND. There, no membership existed to join or decline. Here the residents contribute: the fund is built 'mahalle halkının katkılarıyla' and grown by bağış, donation, which is a voluntary act in Ottoman law and in Kars's usage. THE COMPULSION IS ON THE LEVY, NOT ON THE FUND, and the distinction must be held: the mahalle is compelled to pay its avârız share, and the sandık exists to relieve that compulsion. Coding compulsory would import the tax's character into the institution that relieves it - the reasoning already recorded at avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme MB3. Medium because Kars nowhere states whether a resident could be pressed to contribute.

NOT .NA, AND NOT ANY OF THE THREE ALLOWED VALUES - THIS IS A VOCABULARY GAP AND IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN FORCED. Unlike Kırkçeşme, which was capitalised once and lived on the nema (CN1=.NA), this fund HAS a contribution stream: Gürsoy's sandık aggregates successive endowments across the register series 1491-1828 and Kars reports enrichment 'çeşitli vesilelerle yapılan bağışlarla' - by donations made on various occasions. That is repeated, occasion-triggered, unscheduled accretion. ex-ante-periodic asserts a schedule the sources do not give; ex-ante-lump asserts a single capitalisation the sources contradict; ex-post-assessment asserts contribution after the loss, which is the general-average pattern and not this. See adjudications and logbook 4.
No rule recorded for how a contribution was measured. Kars works from court registrations of completed endowments, which record the sum given and the giver but not an assessment basis.
No enforcement recorded. Non-payment of the avârız was enforceable; failure to endow the sandık is not addressed, and the two must not be run together.

MIXED, on the same enumerated peril list as avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme and from an independent register series. Covariate: 'yangın, deprem, su baskını, salgın hastalık gibi afetler' - fire, earthquake, flood, epidemic. Idiosyncratic: 'fakir, dul ve yetimlerin ihtiyaçları', the needs of the poor, widows and orphans; 'kimsesiz kızların evlendirilmesi', marriage portions for girls without kin; 'sahipsiz cenazelerin masrafları', the funerals of the unclaimed dead; and working capital for those entering trade. Two sources, two corpora, the same mixture - which is evidence that the mixture is the Ottoman quarter fund's design and not one author's list.
Not addressed. Neither author asks whether relief altered the conduct of those relieved, or whether the perils responded to the defence mounted against them.

THE CHARACTERISTIC FAILS ON THIS FORM AND I DECLINE TO FORCE IT. PY0 admits one value; this fund's documented expenditure runs across two. Individual: relief to victims of particular fires, floods, earthquakes and epidemics; the funeral of a particular unclaimed corpse; a marriage portion for particular girls; capital for a particular man entering trade. Collective and non-excludable: the quarter's avârız and nüzul liability itself, and 'su yolu, kaldırım, sıbyan mektebi gibi amme hizmetleri' - water conduits, paving and the primary school (Kars 168) - with Gürsoy 105 giving the same list for the sandıks in his court, 'dini yapıların, eğitim-öğretim kurumlarının, çeşme-suyollarının bakım-onarım ve görevli ücretlerinin karşılanması'. DEPARTURE FROM PRECEDENT, DELIBERATE: avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme was coded individual-indemnity at LOW with a note that the fund outputs both. Repeating that here would understate a form whose NAMED and RECURRING expenditures are predominantly collective, and would manufacture agreement between two rows on the strength of one row's compromise. PY0 has now failed on two Ottoman forms running. See logbook 4.

NO FITTING VALUE, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN EVIDENTIAL. The fund's PRINCIPAL disbursement is the quarter's tax share, which is a scheduled collective obligation and is not a member drawing on a pool at all - it is neither realised-loss, nor life-event, nor rotation, nor need-assessed. The subordinate disbursements then take three of the four values at once: disaster relief is realised-loss, an orphan's marriage portion is life-event, relief of the poor is need-assessed. PY1 has no 'mixed' where VF2 does, so the fact cannot be written down. Contrast confraternity_fund_it PY1, coded realised-loss at low: THERE the dominant function is event-relief and the alternatives are peripheral, so a dominant value with a note is honest; HERE the dominant function is not a payout trigger. The difference between the two cells is the finding, not an inconsistency. See logbook 4.
How relief was allocated among eligible residents is not recorded. Kars's registrations concern endowment, trusteeship and debt, not disbursement procedure.

No cap on any claim is stated. The operative constraint is upstream and budgetary - disbursement was met from the return on the lent capital - but that budgets the fund, it does not cap a claim. Same reading as avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme PY3.

DELIBERATELY NOT FILLED FROM THE OTHER ROW'S SOURCE. Kars says only that 'böyle bir kredi kullanımı sonucunda elde edilecek gelir, vakfın hayır cihetine harcanırdı' - the income from such lending was spent on the waqf's charitable purpose. He does not state the principal-inviolability rule. Küçük does state it for Kırkçeşme, where it is quoted as a principle and carries LS1=capped at high, and it is doctrinally general to para vakıfları, so it very probably held here too. Writing it in on that reasoning would be inference dressed as evidence, and would produce agreement between the two Ottoman rows by construction - the error the friendly_society_england / friendly_society_female_england pair exists in this census to prevent.

Not addressed. Note that .NR here rather than the .NA carried at avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme LS2 is a consequence of CN1: there, .NA propagated from a fund nobody contributed to; here residents do contribute, so the question of a claim on the surplus is live and merely unanswered.

NOT CODED 1, AND THE REASON IS A LOCATOR PROBLEM WORTH THE MAINTAINER'S ATTENTION. There plainly IS liability beyond contribution in this setting, and it is well evidenced: the mahalle is collectively answerable, Kars describing residents 'birbirlerinin davranışlarından dolayı birbirlerine karşı sorumlu', and Papastamatiou states the mechanism for the Ottoman Peloponnese in general terms - the practical value of maktu is 'the collective responsibility which counterbalances the financial embarrassment or insolvency of some members of the community with the proportionate distribution of the taxes to the rest of them'. BUT THAT LIABILITY ATTACHES TO THE TAX, NOT TO THE FUND. LS3 asks whether a member can be pursued beyond what he has contributed or agreed to contribute TO THE POOL, and coding 1 would import the levy's character into the institution that relieves it - the same move refused at MB3. The census has no cell for the residual exposure the pool exists to absorb, which is a real gap and is recorded as an observation, not as a proposed characteristic. See adjudications and logbook 4.

NOT official-adjudication, AND THIS IS A CONSIDERED REFUSAL TO REPEAT avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme's READING. The kadı's court is everywhere in Kars's evidence - trustee appointment and replacement, the accounting of debtors, the boundary dispute between Mercan Ağa and Samanveren mahalleleri over a bakery and serhane - but all of it is the LENDING and ADMINISTRATIVE side. How a claimed loss was established before relief was granted is not addressed. avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme VF1 was coded official-adjudication at HIGH on exactly this kind of lending-side supervision; repeating it here would create agreement between two forms observed through the same record type, which is the record type's bias and not the forms' similarity. I flag the Kırkçeşme cell for review rather than propose a change to it. See logbook 4.

Applicable, because VF1 is .NR and not 'none', and unanswered. What was established before relief was granted - the fact of the disaster, the claimant's need, or his conduct - is exactly the question and the source is silent.

THE CELL THAT SEPARATES THIS ROW FROM avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme, AND IT IS DIRECTLY STATED: 'Mahallelerde kurulan avarız vakıflarının yöneticileri mahalleli tarafından seçilir ve yine mahalleli tarafından mahkemede tescil ettirilirdi' - the administrators of the avarız waqfs founded in the quarters were CHOSEN BY THE RESIDENTS and registered at court BY THE RESIDENTS. Kars then documents the machinery in operation across four registered cases: el-Hac Mehmed ibn-i Kasım of Kızılbey replaced by Sefer Beşe when he left on hajj; Hasan ibn-i Mahmud of Akseki succeeded by Yusuf Efendi with the debtors' accounts drawn up at the handover (Topal Musli 17,000 akçe, Gevher Hatun 6,000); Ali Ağa appointed at Ereğli on the endower's death; el-Hac Abdulfettah of Müftü Ali Çelebi replaced 'ihtiyardır deyu', on the ground that he was aged. Turnover on account of age, death, pilgrimage, absence and neglect of duty, each time through the residents and the court. At Kırkçeşme, GV1 is .NR - a value corrected on 2026-08-13 away from an inference. This is the same institution family answering the question in evidence for the first time.

A waqf in perpetuity, with no terminal date. Gürsoy's register series carries these funds continuously from 1491 to 1828 and records the number of avarız waqfs rising some ninety per cent between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, with eight of the last nine waqfs registered in 1826-1828 being avarız waqfs. Institutional persistence across three centuries is the evidence, not a clause.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA through confidence, articulation, source_ref, source_lang and source_read.

Pledge and surety together, and Kars states the rule and then shows it working. The rule: the waqf money was lent 'kefil ve rehin bırakma esasına riayet edilerek', observing the principle of leaving a guarantor and a pledge, under istiğlal and istirbah. The case: eş-Şeyh Abdurrahman borrowed 300 esedî guruş and gave his house in Sultan Bayezid Mahallesi as rehn-i kavî; when he could not repay, the mütevelli let the house for a full year at 3,600 akçe and set the rent against the debt. Real estate and a solvent guarantor in the same instrument, hence mixed. Medium because Kars gives the norm and one worked instance rather than a series.

Observed absence. The return is a rate, not a price for bearing a peril: 'genellikle kâr haddi %15-20 arasında uygulanmıştır' - the profit rate was generally applied between fifteen and twenty per cent - fixed by the muamele-i şer'iyye framework and the legal ceiling rather than by the borrower's exposure, and security was demanded of everyone alike rather than graded. Agrees with avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme PR1=0, and the agreement is not manufactured: the two rows rest on different registers and reach the same flat legal rate.

Pooling in the ordinary case: members support one another out of resources they have jointly built - 'entrance fees, annual subscriptions, donations, fines, investments in property and land' (175) - and no party outside the association bears the hazard. The clearest instance is the Florentine guild of the oliandoli and pizzicagnoli, which in 1345 'established a separate societas that managed a fund explicitly destined for the support of sick, poor or deceased members' (187). MEDIUM, AND THE RESERVATION IS THE VITERBO CASE, WHICH IS NOT POOLING: in 1196 the 170 members of the confraternity of the farm labourers of Viterbo contracted with the rector of Santa Maria Maddalena for regular payments in return for storage rooms, quarters for sick confreres, at least three members' funerals a year and the social banquets, and Gazzini's own gloss is that 'the individual was not insured, but the group to which the individual belonged was' (181). That is a transfer to a third party for a consideration - spreading inside a membership body, and the census's cleanest candidate for it. Not coded as its own row here; see adjudications.

Occupation, but the value is downstream of the author's own scope decision and that must travel with it: Gazzini writes that she includes religious associations 'only when they were mainly composed of professionals' (173). Within that scope the bodies are trade-based - the Ferrara shoemakers of 1112, the Modena blacksmiths of 1244, the Venetian caulkers, the Florentine oliandoli e pizzicagnoli. Outside it the Italian schola runs straight into confession and locality: the confraternity of Sant'Appiano di Valdelsa is a rural devotional body and the Arzignano confraternita della Vergine mixes artisans with small landowners. Medium, and the comparative-concept hazard is that 'occupation' here reports where Gazzini drew her line.

No numerical restriction recorded. What Gazzini gives is closure of a different kind and in both directions: fifteenth-century Milanese scholae expelled members, who 'consequently lost their identity as confrater as well as all material and spiritual benefits connected to membership', while in Venice 'enrolment in the guild became compulsory for anyone wishing to practise a profession'. Those are facts about exclusion and about compulsion, which are MB3's question and not this one.

Voluntary as the medieval Italian norm, and the exceptions are recorded rather than averaged away. Two run the other way and both are late: Venice, where enrolment became compulsory for anyone wishing to practise (189), and the 1345 Florentine fund, where 'all guild members had to join this society' (187) - though that is compulsion into the FUND conditional on already being in the guild, which is a second-order compulsion and not the same fact. Medium because the trend across the period is toward forced inclusion and this row spans the period.

Contribution falls due before the loss and recurs. Gazzini lists the funding of the segregated assistance funds as 'entrance fees, annual subscriptions, donations, fines, investments in property and land as well as from other financial activities' (175); the Viterbo confreres 'had to make regular payments' (181); the Florentine societas of 1345 carried 'an obligatory payment of 24 denari' (187). Medium rather than high because the mix is heterogeneous - subscription sits beside legacy, fine and rental income - and Gazzini nowhere gives a payment calendar.

Low, and resting on a single figure. The 1345 Florentine societas required 'an obligatory payment of 24 denari' of all guild members, a flat sum and therefore equal rather than graded to stake or capacity. One instance is not a tradition, and Gazzini gives no other contribution schedule. Read as the value of the one documented rule, not of Italian confraternities generally.

Enforceable. Membership of the 1345 Florentine fund was obligatory on guild members and so was its payment (187). More generally, Gazzini treats fines as a standing instrument against members who 'had not fulfilled their duties and obligations', and records that in Venice a third of the fines went to the relief of poor and sick members while Florence split them with the town and Pistoia three ways with the cathedral's building authority (187-188) - a sanction machinery that presupposes compellable duties.

Mixed, and Gazzini's peril list is the widest in the census. Idiosyncratic: illness at home and away, injury, disability, old age, unemployment, death and burial, work-related damage, the theft of a member's livestock at Arzignano, ransom from pirates and bandits, imprisonment for debt. Covariate within a city or a route: insecurity on the trade roads, which the Milanese and Pavian merchant bodies met collectively, and political persecution and banishment in the factional struggles that the Piacenza and Parma statutes of the early fourteenth century wrote into their relief clauses. Medium because the mixture is assembled across a peninsula and three centuries rather than observed in one body.

ADVERSARIAL, AND THIS IS THE SECOND OCCURRENCE OF HZ2=1 IN THE CENSUS. The peril is human predation that answers the defence mounted against it, and the institution is built around that fact. The Milanese mercatores utentes stratis controlled the roads and it fell first to the merchants and subsidiarily to public officials 'to check which roads were safe: a merchant venturing on unapproved roads who fell victim to theft was not eligible for aid from the Chamber of Merchants' (179). Pavia's statutes of 1295 and 1346 protected named land and river routes, required their use, financed their safety from the payments of members and users, and required the magistrate to punish the robatores stratarum. Conventions were then struck with the Malaspina, 'which previously had committed acts of extortion on those who ventured onto their lands' (180) - the adversary is a party one can treat with. Contrast a storm, which cannot be deterred and cannot be negotiated with.

The fund pays individuals: 'help in cases of infirmity and accident', cash benefits, medical and pharmaceutical assistance, hospitalisation, compensation for work-related damages, provision against unemployment and old age, burial, and ransom to pirates and bandits (187). Medium and not high because the same associations also produced a plainly collective good - the Florentine, Piacentine, Modenese and Parmesan hospitals they founded and governed, whose assistance 'was not limited to guild and confraternity members' but 'ensured a minimum of protection to the population' (184). Coded on the FUND rather than on the hospital, and the distinction is Gazzini's: the hospital is a separate institution the guild controls, not the guild's pool.

Relief follows an event that has befallen the member - illness at or away from home, injury, theft of goods or livestock, capture, imprisonment, death. LOW, AND THE LOW IS DOING WORK: two other triggers are attested in the same tradition and PY1 has no 'mixed' to hold them. The Venetian caulkers' veteran places turn on age, a life-event; the Milanese guild of the blind, lame and crippled of 1471 and the confraternities for the disabled distribute on need. The value records the dominant documented trigger and not an exclusive one. The one allocation rule Gazzini gives is not a fund rule: eligible veteran caulkers 'were simply chosen by a draw', which she reads as the guild avoiding a productivity criterion, and the veteran place is an employment quota inside a workshop rather than a payout from a pool.

No cap on the amount of a claim is stated. What is bounded is SCOPE, not quantum, and the boundary is geographical: aid to a member who fell ill away from home ran to a day's walk at Sant'Appiano, extended to two days at Saint Leonardo in Viterbo in the 1140s, ten miles at Imola in 1160, and the whole territory between the Apennines and the Po for the Modena blacksmiths in 1244. A veteran caulker's pension was graded to his physical condition - full salary if still able to work, half if incapacitated (181-182) - which is a benefit schedule and not a cap independent of the loss.

What happened when a fund could not meet its claims is not addressed. Given Gazzini's central finding - that relief was in most cases a reasonable expectation rather than an enforceable right - the question may not have arisen in the form LS1 asks it, but that is a reading and not evidence.

What is established is not that the loss happened but that the claimant did not bring it on himself: 'a merchant venturing on unapproved roads who fell victim to theft was not eligible for aid from the Chamber of Merchants' (179). The theft is not in doubt; the route is. Pavia's statutes make the same test by requiring use of the protected routes (180). NOTE THE DIRECTION OF THE TEST - it is EX ANTE, established against a rule published before the journey, which is what the type row already records from Gazzini's Italian article and what separates this form from guild_box_brabant, where the busmeester's huisbezoek establishes an entitlement after the event. The pairing of an adversarial hazard with fault-based verification is the substantive result of this row.

Collective: guilds and confraternities governed their own funds, and in Florence, Bologna and Perugia governed the city as well. External-administered: 'the statutes of Venetian guilds were largely dictated by public officials, the Giustizieri', so that 'it is hard to say whether the scheme was a private initiative or a public pension scheme', and Gazzini concludes that 'the modern private-public dichotomy that is often inapt to explain phenomena in legal history is thus also in the present context only of limited value' (182). Coding either value would resolve by assertion what the source holds open. .NR here means 'the source refuses the question', which is a different state from silence and which the census's four tokens cannot distinguish - noted in logbook 4.

The 1345 Florentine societas is a standing fund with no terminal date.

Observed absence. The cost of bearing the peril is not set before the event: the 1345 Florentine payment is a flat 24 denari on every guild member, and no contribution in Gazzini's material is graded to a member's exposure, trade, age or route. Her whole argument turns on this - that support was 'crypto-insurance' precisely because members bought a sense of security rather than a priced cover, and that on Sapori's two tests most schemes fail the first, since 'in most cases guild members did not acquire a legally enforceable right to help. They simply developed a reasonable expectation of receiving it.' Medium rather than high because the Viterbo 1196 contract does exchange defined regular payments for defined services, which is the nearest thing to a price in the material - and even there the payment is not graded by peril.
